en.title: FAA expands AI advice to manage air traffic congestion across entire US airspace
en.summary: Airlines praised the AI tool, but the air traffic controllers’ union wasn’t involved.
en.body:
The US government has expanded the use of an AI tool for advising air traffic controllers to assist in managing air traffic across the entire national airspace system. Airline executives have voiced support for the rollout, but the US labor union representing air traffic controllers has said it was not involved in designing or testing the AI-driven system.

The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) says the $875 million SMART system has helped reroute 180 flights since being implemented in airspace over Washington, DC, on September 21. The agency claims that this saved an average of 10 minutes per flight and almost 80 gallons of fuel per flight—and it is apparently hoping such results can be replicated nationwide through the expanded deployment.

“After a successful initial rollout to the National Capital Region in September, the FAA will now use SMART in the airspace of all 22 centers across the country to reduce delays, reduce fuel consumption and improve the travel experience for the flying public,” according to the agency statement posted on November 10.

After launching its Dots AI agents platform earlier this year, OpenAI is launching a wallet for the agents. ChatGPT Wallet is rolling out starting today for ChatGPT Pro subscribers in the US aged 18 and older using a US billing address and "eligible US-issued American Express, Chase, Mastercard and Visa cards."

After adding a card to the wallet, your Dots agents can use it to buy things in response to your prompts, but they'll check in with you each time before checking out. OpenAI's support page says every purchase with ChatGPT Wallet requires a security check with biometric verification like Face ID or a fingerprint scan.

Similar to Grok Bot, Perplexity Teammates are task-oriented proactive agentic AI threads that work for you without constantly being prompted. Meta Muse and ChatGPT Dots are similar, but use a single chat model rather than supporting multiple instances.

Here’s more about Perplexity Teammates :

Teammates are a team of AI agents that own ongoing work. Give a teammate a responsibility, such as managing a growth campaign, triaging incoming bug reports, tracking your metrics, or researching a new market, and it owns that work around the clock. It plans the tasks, brings in more agents when the work grows, and follows through until the result is ready for your review.

Access to Teammates currently requires a paid Perplexity Max subscription. The feature builds on top of Perplexity’s existing AI orchestration system.

en.title: Google now lets people connect Gemini to their bank accounts
en.summary: This is for spending analysis and not for making purchases.
en.body:
This is for spending analysis and not for making purchases.

Google just announced that Gemini users can now connect the chatbot to their bank accounts via integration with Google Wallet . This is not a shopping platform in which chatbots buy stuff on command, like Meta Muse . Rather, it's being pitched as a way for users to "get more tailored responses around personal finance."

Once connected, folks can ask the chatbot questions about their accounts. This could, in theory, help save money by finding unnecessary subscriptions and the like. Google gives an example of the chatbot sussing out a price increase for a particular subscription. This information could already be gleaned by just looking at a bank statement or two, but where would be the fun in that?

Personal Intelligence in Gemini securely connects information from apps you already use to make your experience more personalized and helpful. Today, we're adding Google Wallet to the list of connected apps so you can get more tailored responses in the @GeminiApp around personal...

— Google (@Google) November 13, 2026

The company does give a couple of examples that go above and beyond what one would find by staring at a banking app. Users can ask Gemini to come up with specific budgets for predetermined time periods, complete with "dynamic charts tracking cash flow, asset allocation" and more. It can also reportedly help set up a holiday budget, and it's getting to be that time of the year .

Of course, security is a major concern here. AI chatbots are going to make mistakes every once in a while, and we would all very much like these mistakes to stay far away from our personal finances. This new toolset only lets Gemini read information from accounts and it cannot "move, manage or invest" any money. It's also a completely opt-in experience and it looks like the feature can be turned on and off rather easily via settings .

This integration is rolling out right now across web and mobile. Google says it has also partnered with the fintech company Plaid to help users "unlock deeper insights." The company didn't give any specifics here. Engadget has reached out to Google to inquire about this partnership and will update the post when we hear back.

This is just the latest news involving AI chatbots having access to our money. OpenAI recently unveiled a feature that lets its Dots agents shop on a user's behalf , joining Meta Muse. This kind of thing has already caused a headache in certain sectors of the internet. Companies like United Airlines , Delta and even Amazon have all banned AI agents from shopping on their respective platforms.

en.title: iOS 27.3 adds three new features I’ve used almost every day
en.summary: iOS 27.3 is coming next month , and during the beta so far there are three new features I’ve been using almost every day. more…
en.body:
iOS 27.3 is coming next month , and during the beta so far there are three new features I’ve been using almost every day.

Siri AI in iOS 27 brings major upgrades by providing world knowledge, personal context features, and being more conversational than ever. But one previously announced Siri improvement—an expanded set of actions for Apple apps—didn’t make the cut in iOS 27.0.

Now in iOS 27.3, though, Apple is rolling out its first set of new app actions for Siri AI.

Siri AI has new capabilities across apps like Calendar, Files, Journal, Mail, Maps, Messages, Music, Notes, Photos, Preview, Reminders, Safari, Shortcuts, and Weather. It’s a big step toward making voice-driven computing more powerful on Apple platforms, and I’ve had fun experimenting with everything new Siri can do.

Read more : iOS 27.3 expands Siri AI with many new capabilities across Apple apps

Apple Health gets a big overhaul in iOS 27.3, with a fresh design and new features that utilize Apple Intelligence for more personalized health insights. Per Apple :

The updated experience includes a new Insights tab that surfaces timely, holistic summaries spanning heart, sleep, readiness, fitness, vitals, and cycle tracking data throughout the day. A dedicated For You section delivers intelligent recommendations tailored to a user’s daily habits — such as practical guidance to adjust a wind-down routine following consecutive nights of interrupted sleep. The app pairs data with dynamic health content, offering educational videos and articles featuring Health app clinical experts.

In my testing so far, I’ve especially enjoyed getting up-to-date guidance every day on my health metrics, browsing the deep collection of new educational videos and articles, and understanding all the factors that contribute to longevity. I think Apple is moving the right direction with this update.

Read more : iOS 27.3 adds all-new Apple Health app, details here

If you have an Apple Watch Series 12 or Apple Watch Ultra 4 , iOS 27.3 adds a powerful new feature called Siri Recap that “ambiently takes notes on your conversations throughout your day and creates high-level Apple Intelligence–generated summaries that you can use later to jog your memory.”

Siri Recap functions like an outsourced short-term memory reserve. The data it collects is saved inside the Siri app in a new Recaps tab, where it lives for seven days and is then deleted—unless you manually save a specific recap.

So far in the beta, I’ve found the summaries Siri generates to strike a good balance of being helpful but not too invasive. It reminds me of key details, but there’s nothing I’ve seen that feels overly sensitive or personalized. That may change over time the more I use it, but so far I think this could prove a really valuable feature.

Read more : watchOS 27.3 adds new Apple Watch feature that I absolutely love

Which new iOS 27.3 features have you been enjoying in the beta? Let us know in the comments.

en.title: Export-banned Nvidia chips are behind China’s most powerful AI models — uh-oh, Jensen!
en.summary: New research shows the most advanced AI models from China were trained on banned Nvidia chips.
en.body:
The leading open-weight models developed by Chinese companies were trained on Nvidia chips that the U.S. government restricted from shipping to its largest geopolitical rival, a new research effort claims.

The apparently widespread access to Blackwell GPUs among Chinese frontier labs shows the magnitude of the problem facing the leading chip designer. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang left the company this week after admitting to his affair with Alice Huang, executive of Megaspeed, a company implicated in smuggling Nvidia chips into China. Alice Huang has also been alleged to be an agent of China’s intelligence service.

While Jensen Huang’s relationships with a customer and two employees have drawn the most public interest, Nvidia’s potential corporate liability for export control violations likely factored into its decision to part ways with Huang.

U.S. export controls are intended to protect the country’s leadership in AI capabilities against China, but Huang has long sought to open up that market. Blackwell GPUs are banned from export to China or Chinese-owned firms, while the Trump administration allows Nvidia to export the H200, a less powerful chip, provided shipments take a circuitous shipping route that allows the U.S. to claim a 25% tariff.

Will DePue, a former OpenAI researcher who leads the nonprofit research group Unemployment Labs, analyzed the weights — the unique structure — of large language models released openly by DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, MiniMax, and Ant Group. The weights still reflect the configurations of the chips used to train them, and DePue was able to find compelling evidence that the most closely watched models, including Moonshot’s Kimi’s K3 releases and DeepSeek’s V4 models, bear fingerprints from training on Blackwell chips.

White House technology adviser Michael Kratsios said earlier this year that Moonshot had used export-banned Nvidia chips, citing U.S. intelligence sources. Epoch AI, a nonprofit research organization, estimates that about two million advanced chips entered China in 2024 and 2025 through schemes designed to hide their final destination.

That doesn’t mean that these models were trained entirely on Nvidia chips, or that export control laws were necessarily violated; the chips could have been in an offshore data center, which has proven a popular way for Chinese firms to access compute and driven an industrial revolution in Malaysia. Epoch’s data estimates that 275,000 Nvidia AI accelerators were imported to Malaysia in 2024 and 2025.

However, the ostensible goal of the export bans is to prevent exactly that: Chinese AI labs training on the most powerful chips. China hawks have long called for stronger controls on who uses chips, not just who owns them or where they are installed.

“If we care about the U.S. tech edge, it doesn’t make any sense to me that you would not allow Chinese companies to access chips in mainland China or Hong Kong and Macau, but then say, actually, if you just go over to Malaysia, you can do whatever you want,” Sam Bresnick, a researcher at the Georgetown Center for Security and Emerging Technology, told TechCrunch this summer.

Megaspeed, the company led by Alice Huang, has been at the center of that trade for several years through its subsidiary Speedmatrix, and has been the subject of investigations by both the U.S. and S i ngaporean government. Friday, Bloomberg also reported that a company with links to Alice Huang was involved in smuggling banned Nvidia chips to a data center in Shanghai.

In May, the short-selling research firm Culper published a report arguing that Nvidia had a “ China problem ” because a significant share of its revenue was driven by Chinese demand, either through remote data centers or smuggling in violation of U.S. law. It detailed Megaspeed’s relationship with Nvidia and alleged that Alice Huang’s companies are backed by Chinese firms that are barred from accessing U.S. chips.

Ironically, short-seller Culper’s bet against Nvidia wasn’t driven by the expectation of a U.S. government crackdown. Instead, it was focused on the Chinese government’s response to the bans, which was to recommit to its domestic chip industry.

If China succeeds, billions of dollars in Chinese demand for Nvidia chips could dry up. Some 600,000 H200 chips are reportedly stockpiled in Hong Kong, awaiting shipment into China. While Chinese companies might want the chips, observers have no consensus on why they haven’t been cleared for import.

Graham Webster, a research scholar at Stanford who focuses on U.S.-China technology policy, said he doesn’t buy the idea that holding the chips back would drive domestic production, since demand for chips is so large. Other theories for the hold-up include preparation for a potential trade deal that would involve importing a large volume of U.S. goods, or concerns about potential surveillance technology in the chips.

For now, U.S. companies have limited obligations to track what their customers do with controlled goods like AI chips. However, Jensen Huang’s personal and professional entanglements with Alice Huang create a much bigger problem for Nvidia if government investigators confirm that chip smuggling took place and that he was aware of it. Nvidia and Huang have both vouched for Megaspeed’s data centers, saying Nvidia officials had visited them to confirm they were legitimate.

The U.S. government’s treatment of Nvidia and Megaspeed is also under scrutiny. Secretary of Commerce Howard Lutnick, who oversees the agencies that license chip exports, could reportedly lose his job after reports that his investigators failed to uncover suspicious chip buyers and were too cozy with Nvidia officials.

en.title: OpenAI board member worries an AI "takeover" of society could be months away
en.summary: Researcher traces a path from AI reward hacking to potential human extinction.
en.body:
How do you think you're going to die?

If you go by the current statistics for deaths in the US , it's reasonable to expect that cancer or heart disease will eventually get you. But OpenAI Foundation board member and Alignment Research Center Executive Director Paul Cristiano thinks we should all be worried about another major mortality risk. Speaking at a lecture series this week , Cristiano bluntly told the audience in a Toronto Convention Center, "I think for most people in this room, the most likely reason they will die is because of an AI accident."

In the opening lecture of a three-part series , Cristiano outlined his worries about the risk of an impending "AI takeover." He defined that as a situation where goal-pursuing AI systems "call the shots in the same sense that humans today call the shots and what happens on Earth" and where any human trying to stop them "would be as ineffective as if you or me was trying to stop the US military." Such a situation would likely lead to mass death and perhaps uninhabitable environments for humans, Cristiano said.

en.title: You can now tempt fate and give your banking information to ChatGPT
en.summary: The new Wallet feature will allow its AI agents to make purchases on your behalf.
en.body:
The new Wallet feature will allow its AI agents to make purchases on your behalf.

OpenAI just announced ChatGPT Wallet , a payment feature that enables its newly-released Dots AI agents to make purchases on behalf of users. Of course, that requires handing over your payment information to a chatbot, which carries some risk . OpenAI says that users only have to input card information once and then it's good to go.

The company has built some guardrails into the system to help attract those wary of letting hallucination-prone chatbots handle their personal finances. First of all, the bots are allowed to run loose and gather up stuff to purchase, but the human has to finalize everything.

Now your dot can securely complete purchases on your behalf—with your approval.

With ChatGPT Wallet, agents pay without access to your actual card details. Every purchase requires a security check.

ChatGPT Wallet is rolling out starting today to dots, for Pro subscribers in the... pic.twitter.com/EhtEZNaKnt

— ChatGPT (@ChatGPT) November 13, 2026

Each purchase has to be approved via a security check like Face ID or a fingerprint scan, similar to how Meta Muse operates . An approval reportedly "creates a clear record of the purchase" which could help with dispute mitigation down the line. The store doesn't receive the actual card information, but rather is provided a "payment token" which is a "substitute for the user's actual card details."

OpenAI has partnered with American Express, Mastercard and Visa for this endeavor. The company promises that this program allows cardholders to maintain their current credit card rewards points and protections.

"Our goal here is to really focus on merchants and our network partners and start building out a really great foundation that's safe and easy to use," Chaya Nayak, who leads product for monetization and payments at OpenAI, told CNBC .

The company is not taking a cut of any purchases made through the system just yet. That should help keep prices low, for now, though it'll most certainly become a revenue stream for OpenAI down the line. We all know modern tech companies like to take the "drug dealer" approach to things. It'll be cheap or free at first until the company slams down the cost hammer in a year or two. Remember how affordable Uber used to be ?

ChatGPT Wallet is rolling out right now, though only to US-based Pro subscribers aged 18 and older. The company promises that it'll "work with businesses, banks and payment networks to learn from early use and expand availability" in the future.

The influx of AI agents running around and making purchases on their own has certainly caused some hiccups in certain corners of the internet. Many companies are outright banning the use of these agents to make purchases, such as Delta and United Airlines . Amazon is doing the same thing , but probably less out of an abundance of caution and more out of jealousy that its own chatbots aren't quite there yet .

One last thing. Why are these AI shopping agents so cute? They always look like Pixar characters or something. It's a bit creepy.

en.title: Windows 0-day dropped by disgruntled researcher hands hackers System rights
en.summary: "SignDrop" exploit lets local users gain all-powerful System rights.
en.body:
Nightmare Eclipse, the pseudonym of a researcher with an ongoing, very public beef with Microsoft, has dropped yet another Windows zero-day.

On Tuesday, Nightmare Eclipse disclosed SignDrop, a vulnerability that gives local users full System rights on some versions of Windows. The vulnerability resides in the Common Log File System , which Microsoft describes as a “general-purpose logging service used by software clients running in user-mode or kernel-mode.” By forcing a privileged process such as Windows Defender to open a crafted CLFS container, an attacker with ordinary user rights can abuse the privileged file creation to elevate privileges to System.

The attack exploits the interaction of CLFS, Windows Defender, and Windows file permissions. The exploit uses Windows Defender to open a log file created by a standard user by calling ServerMpUpdateEngineSignature, a legitimate Defender function for processing antivirus signature updates.

en.title: ChatGPT’s new Wallet lets AI agents shop and check out for you
en.summary: ChatGPT Wallet lets AI agents shop and check out on users' behalf, starting with a limited rollout to U.S. Pro subscribers.
en.body:
ChatGPT can now shop for you. On Friday, OpenAI launched a new wallet feature that lets its agents, called dots , help you decide what to buy and then complete the purchase on your behalf. The option will initially be available to a limited number of U.S. ChatGPT Pro subscribers, ages 18 and up, with a U.S.-issued Visa, Mastercard, or American Express.

OpenAI says that users are fully in control of the purchases, as they’re able to review the items, the total, and the payment card that will be used to complete the transaction before the checkout occurs. In addition, users will approve the purchases directly with a security check like Face ID or a fingerprint, which creates a record of their transaction.

The addition comes as consumer-facing AI tools are working to find the right product-market fit, in terms of how they can help people be more efficient as they complete various tasks. While companies like DoorDash and Uber have so far reported low numbers of orders placed by AI agents, Meta’s Muse, which now has over 10 million users, has seen AI-assisted shopping become a top activity on its app.

Other personal AI agents, like Instinct, also support making purchases on users’ behalf.

It’s no surprise, then, that OpenAI would want to enter this space more with an agentic shopping feature of its own.

To get started, ChatGPT subscribers add their eligible payment cards to the new ChatGPT Wallet, then ask their dot to help with a purchase. (This setup is a one-time thing; users don’t have to re-enter their payment information every time they buy.) When it’s time to transact, ChatGPT’s Wallet charges the selected card using a payment token, which is a substitute for the user’s actual card details, so that information isn’t shared with either the dot or the merchant.

The merchant will automatically receive what it needs to fulfill the order from the dot, like the shipping address and contact information, OpenAI says. The company notes that customers who shop via their dots will still be able to earn their credit card rewards and be able to take advantage of protections that typically come with cards, like being able to dispute transactions.

The limited availability at launch will allow OpenAI to test and improve the feature and its capabilities before rolling it out more broadly. In the future, the company plans to offer users more control over the feature by allowing them to set spending limits or configure other parameters around purchase categories or time periods, so they can pre-approve purchases that their agent can then handle more autonomously.

It also aims to make the agentic shopping feature an option at a broader number of supported retailers. This could be a challenge in some areas, where retailers are blocking AI agents from using their site ; on the shopping front, the largest retailer to ban AI agents is Amazon, as it aims to steer users to its own AI agent, Alexa, instead.

To help retailers adapt to agentic commerce, OpenAI also published a Commerce Partner Playbook that offers tools and guidance to sites that want to support customers using agents.

en.title: The unfolding Jensen Huang scandal: a timeline
en.summary: Jensen Huang has resigned from Nvidia following an affair, which could have ramifications for national security as the U.S. and China race to develop the most advanced AI infrastructure.
en.body:
Nvidia co-founder and now former CEO Jensen Huang has never been as prone to controversy as AI leaders like OpenAI’s Sam Altman or SpaceXAI’s Elon Musk. But the 63-year-old industry kingpin recently admitted that he cheated on his wife of 40 years in affairs that could have ramifications beyond Huang’s personal life and U.S. national security.

U.S. officials believe that one of Huang’s likely romantic interests, Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, is a Chinese spy who has been feeding information back to Beijing. (Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen, is of no relation to Jensen Huang.)

Megaspeed is a Singapore-based AI infrastructure company that reportedly purchased $4.8 billion worth of Nvidia chips over the last two years. The U.S. and Singapore have both previously investigated Megaspeed over suspicions that the firm was illegally sharing chips with China. The Justice Department has since taken over the federal investigation into the company, The New York Times has reported.

The story took a sudden turn on Wednesday. Citing five people who worked at Nvidia, the Times reported that Huang also had an extramarital relationship with Kimberly Powell, the company’s vice president of healthcare, who reports directly to him. Nvidia, Huang and Powell have not confirmed the report. Reached by a Times reporter, Huang reportedly said, “I don’t think you should be talking to me directly,” before hanging up.

By early Thursday morning, Huang was no longer CEO of the company he co-founded 33 years ago. Then, Thursday afternoon, Reuters dropped another bombshell, publishing a report alleging that Huang had yet another extramarital affair with another unnamed Nvidia employee.

The U.S. and China are embroiled in a fierce technological arms race to build the most advanced AI infrastructure, which could shape each country’s economic future, military prowess, and capacity for innovation. Nvidia is valuable in this competition as one of the world’s largest makers of AI chips, which are essential for accelerating AI development. But as an American company, Nvidia faces government restrictions on the sale of its most powerful chips to Chinese entities.

As the controversy unfolds, we are organizing the most relevant events into a reverse-chronological timeline to keep you up to date.

More reports continue to roll out that illustrate the shock and severity of Huang’s resignation from Nvidia.

Bloomberg reported that Huang looked “broken and shattered, his legendary energy depleted” by the time he surrendered his role on Wednesday night, uttering phrases like “whatever” and “I don’t care.”

Separately, the Wall Street Journal reported that Huang had been critical of his CFO and current interim CEO, Colette Kress. Huang is said to have described Kress as “a deer in the headlights” during a presentation this summer, and he had described Kress as someone who could not help him steer strategy or decision-making.

In a scathing letter sent to Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, Representative Richard Neal (D-MA) and Senator Ron Wyden (D-OR) said they will investigate how the Trump administration handled Nvidia’s chip sales to China, especially after Trump was briefed about Huang’s relationship with a purported Chinese spy.

“Although [Lutnick] and President Trump were reportedly briefed on this intelligence, the Administration did not appear to acknowledge this evident national security threat. On the contrary: despite reportedly learning of Mr. Huang’s compromising relationship last fall, President Trump granted Nvidia permission to sell its advanced H200 AI chips to China in December 2025 in exchange for a cut of the export sales,” the letter states.

That same evening, Senator Tim Scott (R-SC) requested that Huang and Lutnick both testify before the Senate Banking Committee.

“The American people deserve answers,” Scott wrote on X.

After Huang was already ousted from Nvidia, we continued to learn more incriminating claims about the former CEO. According to Reuters, Huang had a third affair with an additional, unnamed employee of Nvidia.

Nvidia said its board had accepted Huang’s resignation on Wednesday. The company’s current CFO, Colette Kress , will take over as interim CEO while still fulfilling her CFO duties. Nvidia is expected to conduct a larger search to determine a permanent successor to Huang.

Harvey C. Jones, a managing partner of Square Wave Ventures and former CEO of Synopsys, was appointed as the company’s first-ever chair of the board of directors. Jones has been on Nvidia’s board since 1993.

Later in the day, Huang confirmed that he would testify in Congress at some point before Thanksgiving, which falls on November 26.

“Jensen and I have been very at odds as some of you already know on export controls, but Nvidia is a very important company to the United States of America,” House Foreign Affairs Committee Chairman Brian Mast said to reporters. “I don’t want to see anything hurt in Nvidia, but he has some very serious questions to answer.”

The testimony is expected to take place behind closed doors, but Mast believes the briefing will be recorded and transcribed.

After reports of a second extramarital affair, Nvidia’s board reportedly plans to meet to discuss Huang’s future at the company, per The Wall Street Journal. Stock fell about 8% in after-hours trading on Wednesday and is down 11% in the past five days.

Huang famously delegates very little and has about 60 direct reports, he has said . The company has not had an obvious successor or a succession plan.

The New York Times reported that Jensen Huang also had an affair with Nvidia vice president of healthcare Kimberly Powell, who reports directly to the CEO.

According to the report, Huang and Powell were captured on film “being affectionate” at a hotel during a conference earlier this year.

Huang has not responded to a request from three Republican congressmen to appear for a closed-door briefing for questioning about his affair with an alleged Chinese spy. House China Committee Chairman John Moolenaar said Wednesday on Fox Business that if Huang doesn’t agree to the briefing, he’ll likely be subpoenaed .

The Nvidia CEO pulled out of upcoming speaking engagements at the ElevenLabs Summit and Anthropic CEO Forum.

Alice Huang and her family reportedly built a network of companies in China and Singapore to acquire Nvidia chips, including founding a Chinese company called Shanghai Century Litong. Founded in 2023, it became an Nvidia-preferred cloud partner, giving it priority access to chips, The Information reported . The Information also reported that Shanghai Century Litong facilitated buying $7.5 billion worth of Nvidia’s chips, including banned chips.

Nvidia’s head lawyer, Tim Teter, intervened in a 2025 U.S. government probe surrounding the suspected smuggling of AI chips by Megaspeed International, Bloomberg reported . Teter contacted Commerce Under Secretary Jeffrey Kessler asking questions about whether the Trump administration played a role in detaining Alice Huang.

In early 2025, Alice Huang and a business partner sought China-based investors for an Asian data center, promising they had no problem in securing GPUs, the Financial Times reported.

On Sunday night, President Trump weighed in on Huang’s controversy and showed support for the Nvidia CEO.

“I have not spoken to him about it. I just know he’s a fine person, but you never know what’s going on,” Trump said.

When asked if Huang should remain chief of Nvidia , Trump said, “I think so. Oh yeah, sure.”

Jensen Huang wrote in a letter to Nvidia employees — which was also published as a press release — that he cheated on his wife.

“I owe my family and all of you an apology,” Huang told his company. “I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry.”

Huang did not mention Alice Huang by name in the message, but linked his infidelity to “the national security concerns raised in news reports.”

“Nvidia’s Board of Directors has initiated an independent investigation. I support the investigation and will cooperate fully. I love our country and our company. I am committed to protecting Nvidia and supporting America’s national security. I am proud and grateful to be an American,” Huang wrote.

Nvidia shares slid over 5% the following day.

Three Republican congressmen — Chairman John Moolenaar of the House Select Committee on China, Chairman Brian Mast of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, and Chairman Rick Crawford of the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence — sent a request to Huang for a closed-door joint briefing with their three committees.

“Recent reports raise significant national security concerns regarding the [People’s Republic of China]’s access to sensitive U.S. technology and information,” the chairmen wrote . “The issue of PRC infiltration and access to cutting-edge U.S. technology is core to the investigative work of our three committees this Congress. It is vital that Congress determines the extent to which U.S. national security has been placed at risk.”

U.S. officials had been investigating Alice Huang and Megaspeed for more than a year when the New York Times broke the story in late October that the two executives also had a close relationship.

An Nvidia spokesperson denied that this relationship was something out of the ordinary.

“Jensen’s interactions with Ms. Huang are not unusual or unexpected. Meetings with customers are part of a CEO’s job; Jensen talks with thousands of customer executives every year,” Nvidia spokesperson John Rizzo said. He added that “if the U.S. government believes that any person is a threat to American industry, it would let us know.”

U.S. officials circulated a secret memo among policymakers that warned that Megaspeed’s Alice Huang, who had a relationship with Jensen Huang, was a spy for China’s Ministry of State Security. This memo was not public knowledge until it was later reported by the New York Times.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio supervised the drafting of the memo.

Around the same time, per the New York Times’ report , U.S. President Donald Trump was briefed about intelligence findings that possible Chinese spy Alice Huang had formed a close relationship with Jensen Huang. Trump did not act on this information.

The Nvidia CEO, an ally of Trump , has repeatedly advocated for the U.S. government to let Nvidia expand its business in China.

Megaspeed was confirmed to be under investigation by both the U.S. and Singaporean governments in October 2025. As a customer of Nvidia, Megaspeed was suspected of helping Chinese companies get around American embargoes on chip exports.

Megaspeed, a neocloud that used Nvidia chips, had been renting computing power to Chinese internet giant Alibaba and other Chinese companies, the Times reported. A Commerce Department official who had visited Megaspeed’s data center in Malaysia in 2024 had found a hoard of Nvidia equipment that was still packed in boxes and the concern was that this equipment was being directly shipped somewhere else, like China, rather than installed and sold as a cloud service.

Jensen Huang had been spotted socializing with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang as early as 2024 in Taiwan, where the Nvidia CEO was born.

These investigations into Megaspeed highlighted concerns about the degree to which Nvidia is able to track its chip exports. At the time, an Nvidia spokesperson told press that the company did not have “any reason to believe products had been diverted.”

“NVIDIA visited multiple Megaspeed sites yet again earlier this week and confirmed what we previously observed — Megaspeed is running a small commercial cloud, like many other companies throughout the world, as allowed by U.S. export control rules,” the Nvidia spokesperson said at the time.

en.title: The Motorola Signature 27 is a beast
en.summary: Motorola's latest phone has a monstrous tandem OLED display, a huge 7,000mah battery, fancy cameras and a massive $1,600 price tag.
en.body:
It’s got a monstrous tandem OLED display, a huge 7,000mAh battery, fancy cameras and a massive $1,600 price tag.

The Motorola Signature 27 is slated to be the first phone on sale in the US to feature Qualcomm's next top-tier processor — the Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 . That alone would make the handset notable. But when you factor in a ton of other high-end hardware including a gorgeous tandem OLED display, a massive silicon-carbon battery and triple rear cameras with a dedicated action sensor, the Signature 27 becomes a powerhouse of a phone.

In some respects, it feels like Motorola's design process was simply to take every fancy component it could get its hands on and shove it in the Signature 27. The phone features a big 6.8-inch Extreme AMOLED Duo display, which is based on the same tandem OLED tech Apple used in the new ProLED MacBook Pro . Unsurprisingly, it looks awesome. Colors are super saturated and it has a ridiculous peak brightness of 12,000 nits, though I couldn't fully test that during my evening demo session. To put that number into context, the peak brightness of the Galaxy S26 Ultra is merely 2,600 nits, and that panel is still super easy to view outdoors. And then over the top of the display, Moto went with Corning's latest Gorilla Glass Ceramic 3.

Around back, the Signature 27's rear cameras are based around a 50-megapixel Sony LYTIA L910 sensor for its main camera. There's also a 50MP ultra-wide camera and a high-res 200MP telephoto camera with a 3x optical zoom. Now, those three alone would be a pretty formidable kit, and when I got a chance to take a telephoto picture of the NYC skyline at sunset, I was rather impressed at how sharp and detailed the final image looked. This is coming from someone who has often lamented Moto's inability to keep up with Apple, Samsung and Google on previous releases. When I used the main camera to take a shot at dusk, I was really pleased with the 27's low-light sensitivity and dynamic range.

The 27's photo kit doesn't stop there. There's actually a fourth EVS sensor — which the company claims is a first in a smartphone — designed to detect pixel-level changes in light to help the phone snap extremely sharp action pics. Sadly, I didn't get to test this feature out in-depth, but it could be a really powerful solution for capturing sports without needing to lug a proper camera around. It could also be a great tool for all the parents who can't get their kids to sit still for a photo.

Meanwhile, on the inside, in addition to a Qualcomm Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 chip, the phone also features 12GB of memory and 512GB of base storage. And if that's not enough, Moto has included a nifty RAM boost that effectively doubles the memory to 24GB to improve things like multitasking. Furthermore, to help deliver strong sustained performance, the 27 features a large 3D vapor chamber (8,384mm²) with what Moto claims is diamond-infused thermal gel to pull heat away from its processor.

Perhaps the best upgrade on the Signature for power users is the move to a huge 7,000 mAh silicon-carbon battery, which dwarfs pretty much anything else on sale in the US right now. Naturally, its charging speeds are pretty rapid too, with up to 90 watts wired or 50 watts wirelessly. The caveat is that you'll need to rely on one of Motorola's proprietary TurboPower adapters. Sadly, the 27 doesn't have built-in magnets either, so if you want support for magnetic accessories, you'll need a case.

Really, every component on the phone is high-end in some way. That's even true of its audio, which is composed of speakers tuned by Bang & Olufsen. I must admit, I'm pretty fond of the phone's general design as well. In addition to your standard lock button and volume rocker, there's a dedicated AI button that can also be customized to open an app of your choosing. The olive green model sports a nifty finish that reminds me of a mix between cloth and leather, while the coal smoke variant features a "tactical weave" reminiscent of ballistic nylon. Even its dust and water resistance is top-notch thanks to an IP69 rating that's good enough for submersion of up to five feet for up to 30 minutes.

However, the design trait I like the most is the way the back of the phone subtly rises to meet all those rear cameras, resulting in a sloping rear panel that leaves all of its lenses basically flush against the back of the phone. There's no big protrusion or bump for stuff to get caught on. That said, with four lenses in back plus a dedicated flash, the Signature 27 is quickly beginning to look like one of those Light L16 cameras from nearly a decade ago. At this point, I have to wonder if it might be easier, and better looking, to go with a more visor-like approach similar to what Google did on the Pixel 6.

Over the past few years, there has been demand for a proper Motorola flagship phone that can truly rival the fancy handsets from Samsung, Apple and Google. With the Signature 27, it really feels like the company took that message to heart. This phone has practically everything you could ask for in a super premium handset, and then some. The downside is that all of this comes with a similarly super premium price tag of $1,600. But if you want an absolute monster of a phone and don't want to wait for next year when more devices get their own Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 chip, keep an eye out when pre-orders go live on November 19.

en.title: Use Photo Tracking in ZoomText to Jump to the Objects in a Picture
en.summary: Have you ever opened a photo and wanted to know right away who’s in it, or spot the dog in the corner, or see what’s on the dinner plate? If you use magnification, you know how that usually goes. You zoom in, pan across the picture bit by bit, and hope you don’t miss what …
en.body:
Have you ever opened a photo and wanted to know right away who’s in it, or spot the dog in the corner, or see what’s on the dinner plate? If you use magnification, you know how that usually goes. You zoom in, pan across the picture bit by bit, and hope you don’t miss what you’re looking for. It works, but it takes time and patience.

Photo Tracking, new in ZoomText 2027, makes this much easier. Instead of scanning every corner of an image, you can go straight to the things that matter to you. Let’s take a look at what it does and how to get started.

Photo Tracking identifies people, animals, food, and other objects in an image. Then it moves the magnified view directly from one object to the next. You no longer need to zoom and pan across the whole picture to find what you want. Photo Tracking takes you right to it.

Photo Tracking is available in ZoomText Magnifier/Reader, ZoomText Magnifier, and Fusion.

Pictures are everywhere: on web pages, in Word documents and PDFs, and in your own photo collection. Photo Tracking helps you get to the parts of an image you care about quickly, so you spend less time searching and more time enjoying or using what you find.

There’s another big benefit. All recognition happens locally on your computer. That means Photo Tracking works offline, and it’s suitable for secure environments where images can’t be sent to an online service.

Getting started takes just a few steps:

Tip: You can also set Photo Tracking to analyze the active window automatically.

Photo Tracking sorts the objects it finds into ten categories:

It starts with your favorite categories, which are Animals and People by default. If you’d rather start somewhere else, you can change your favorites in Photo Tracking Settings.

Use these keystrokes while you explore an image:

When you zoom in or out with CAPS LOCK+UP ARROW , CAPS LOCK+DOWN ARROW , or CAPS LOCK+ENTER while using Photo Tracking, ZoomText announces the new magnification level, so you always know where you are.

For complete hotkeys and settings, see the Photo Tracking help topic in ZoomText. To learn more about Photo Tracking and other ZoomText 2027 features, visit What’s New in ZoomText 2027 .

Give Photo Tracking a try the next time you come across a picture. We think you’ll enjoy how quickly you can find what you’re looking for.

Have questions? Send an email to training@vispero.com .

es.title: LiDAR en los teléfonos móviles: una tecnología que podría ayudar a las personas ciegas a detectar escaleras y desniveles
es.summary: Los avances en tiflotecnología no siempre requieren desarrollar nuevos dispositivos. En ocasiones, el potencial está en aprovechar tecnologías que ya incorporan herramientas de uso cotidiano, como los teléfonos inteligentes. Es el caso del sistema experimental desarrollado por investigadores de la Universidad de Iowa (Estados Unidos), que utiliza el sensor LiDAR de un teléfono móvil para […] La entrada LiDAR en los teléfonos móviles: una tecnología que podría ayudar a las personas ciegas a detectar escaleras y desniveles se publicó primero en Conticgo .
es.body:
Los avances en tiflotecnología no siempre requieren desarrollar nuevos dispositivos. En ocasiones, el potencial está en aprovechar tecnologías que ya incorporan herramientas de uso cotidiano, como los teléfonos inteligentes.

Es el caso del sistema experimental desarrollado por investigadores de la Universidad de Iowa (Estados Unidos), que utiliza el sensor LiDAR de un teléfono móvil para detectar escaleras y cambios de altura en el terreno en tiempo real.

La investigación, publicada el 2 de octubre de 2026 en la revista científica Scientific Reports , demuestra que es posible utilizar el sensor de profundidad de un smartphone comercial para identificar determinados riesgos durante los desplazamientos, sin necesidad de incorporar cámaras externas ni hardware especializado.

LiDAR es una tecnología que permite medir distancias y obtener información tridimensional del entorno mediante pulsos de luz láser.

Algunos teléfonos inteligentes, como determinados modelos de iPhone Pro, incorporan sensores LiDAR que permiten detectar la profundidad de los objetos y construir representaciones tridimensionales de los espacios.

Aunque esta tecnología se utiliza habitualmente en fotografía, aplicaciones de realidad aumentada y mediciones de espacios, también ofrece posibilidades interesantes en el ámbito de la accesibilidad.

En este caso, los investigadores han aprovechado esa capacidad para identificar irregularidades en el suelo, especialmente escaleras y cambios de altura que pueden pasar desapercibidos durante los desplazamientos de una persona ciega o con baja visión.

El sistema desarrollado utiliza un iPhone 17 Pro Max con iOS 26.2 y el sensor LiDAR integrado en el dispositivo.

Su funcionamiento se basa en analizar la representación tridimensional del entorno que genera el teléfono. A partir de esa información, un algoritmo proyecta ocho líneas virtuales en diferentes direcciones para identificar cambios geométricos en la superficie.

Cuando detecta una variación compatible con una escalera o un desnivel, el sistema puede generar una alerta para advertir al usuario.

Una de las características más interesantes es que el procesamiento se realiza directamente en el teléfono, sin necesidad de enviar las imágenes a servidores externos ni utilizar procesamiento en la nube.

El algoritmo analiza la información a una frecuencia de 60 imágenes por segundo, lo que permite detectar cambios en el entorno con una respuesta prácticamente inmediata.

Para comprobar el funcionamiento del sistema, los investigadores realizaron 120 pruebas en ocho ubicaciones diferentes, utilizando escaleras con distintas alturas y pendientes.

Los ensayos contemplaron diferentes condiciones de iluminación, tanto en interiores como en exteriores, y aproximaciones a las escaleras desde arriba y desde abajo.

Los resultados fueron los siguientes:

Los investigadores también observaron diferencias según la dirección de aproximación. La detección fue menos eficaz cuando el usuario se acercaba a las escaleras desde arriba, algo especialmente relevante porque los desniveles descendentes pueden resultar difíciles de identificar mediante sensores de profundidad.

Es importante interpretar estos resultados con cautela: las pruebas fueron realizadas por un único operador entrenado y no incluyeron participantes ciegos o con baja visión. Además, no se llevaron a cabo ensayos específicos en recorridos sin obstáculos para establecer una tasa de falsas alarmas fiable.

Por tanto, los resultados demuestran la viabilidad técnica del sistema, pero todavía no permiten afirmar que esté preparado para su utilización autónoma en situaciones reales.

Una de las ventajas de esta investigación es que no requiere desarrollar un dispositivo completamente nuevo.

El sistema aprovecha un sensor LiDAR que ya está integrado en determinados teléfonos comerciales. Esto abre la posibilidad de explorar aplicaciones de asistencia visual utilizando hardware que algunas personas ya tienen a su disposición.

No obstante, es importante señalar que no todos los smartphones incorporan LiDAR. Además, el algoritmo desarrollado depende de las características del sensor y del entorno de programación utilizado, por lo que no puede trasladarse automáticamente a cualquier teléfono.

Los investigadores consideran necesario ampliar las pruebas, incorporar diferentes dispositivos y evaluar el funcionamiento del sistema con personas ciegas y con baja visión antes de plantear su utilización como herramienta de movilidad.

La detección de escaleras y desniveles continúa siendo uno de los desafíos de la movilidad para las personas con discapacidad visual.

Aunque el bastón blanco es una herramienta fundamental para detectar obstáculos y explorar el espacio próximo, determinadas situaciones pueden requerir información adicional sobre las características del terreno.

La utilización de sensores de profundidad en teléfonos móviles podría abrir nuevas posibilidades para complementar las ayudas técnicas existentes, proporcionando información adicional sobre el entorno y anticipando determinados riesgos.

Sin embargo, estas tecnologías todavía necesitan demostrar su fiabilidad en condiciones reales y no deben considerarse sustitutas del bastón blanco ni de la formación en orientación y movilidad.

La investigación demuestra que los sensores LiDAR de los teléfonos inteligentes tienen un potencial que va mucho más allá de la fotografía y la realidad aumentada. Su aplicación en el ámbito de la tiflotecnología podría contribuir al desarrollo de herramientas más accesibles, económicas y fáciles de integrar en dispositivos cotidianos.

Si te ha gustado esta noticia no te pierdas las últimas novedades en tiflotectnología en nuestro apartado de noticias y redes sociales .

Fuentes: Estudio científico completo

en.title: In-Process 13th November 2026
en.summary: This week, we’ve updated NVDA, and some documentation, we hear from our user group in Japan, plus there are tips for File Explorer and more! NVDA 2026.3.1 Updated VPAT / ACR NVDA on show in Japan Unassigned gestures File Explorer shortcuts NVDA 2026.3.1 NV Access is pleased to announce that version 2026.3.1 of NVDA, the… Read More
en.body:
This week, we’ve updated NVDA, and some documentation, we hear from our user group in Japan, plus there are tips for File Explorer and more!

NV Access is pleased to announce that version 2026.3.1 of NVDA , the free screen reader for Microsoft Windows, is now available for download. We encourage all users to upgrade to this version.

Highlights This is a patch release to fix security issues. A bug fix is also included for an issue introduced in 2026.3 with the task switcher in Windows 10. The Brazilian Portuguese eSpeak voice was restored to the behaviour in 2026.2.

Read the full changes and download at the NVDA 2026.3.1 release announcement .

We’ve updated our VPAT. Actually we’ve updated our ACR , but whatever you call it, there’s a new one. Mostly of interest to companies who use NVDA and need to keep a copy on file for any software they use, the activity of completing it is useful, even for us as a screen reader manufacturer. VPAT stands for Voluntary Product Accessibility Template – it’s a large document which gives you points to consider and rate your software and website on many aspects of accessibility. VPAT is technically the blank template. The Accessibility Conformance Report (ACR) is the completed report about a product.

NVDA is, as you would expect, quite good at all the things someone who is blind might need. However, through this process, over the years, we have previously identified and fixed several issues which may affect other users. The newest version of this document doesn’t dramatically change any of our ratings or identify or fix any new issues, but it is up to date for NVDA 2026.3.1. So, if your organisation needs a copy, head over to the VPAT section of the Corporate and Government page and you’ll find it there.

We love to hear from our communities all around the world. There is a very active community of users, and contributors in Japan. They have a website devoted to the local community: https://www.nvda.jp/ and recently attended the Sight World 2026 conference in Tokyo https://www.sight-world.com/sightworld2026

Nobuyuki and the team presented at the conference on four main themes: Screen sharing using Copilot Add-on Store NVDA Coach New Forms of Learning with NVDA

They wrote to advise us that the event was a huge success, and they had around 100 people in attendance at their presentation. They sent us photographs and a link to their video presentation:

The Video is in Japanese, and includes a message from NV Access Training & Support manager Quentin Christensen (in English).

A banner from the NVDA Japanese Team session titled “NVDAではじめる、新しい「学び」のかたち” (“A New Form of ‘Learning’ Starting with NVDA”), presented at Sight World 2026 in Tokyo.

Unassigned gestures The last couple of releases I’ve highlighted the unassigned gestures, so let’s do that again. Unassigned gestures are things which you can do with a keystroke or touch action etc, but we didn’t set one up by default. There are only two this time around: Magnifier: A new unassigned command has been added to move the mouse cursor to the center of the magnified view. Added an unassigned Quick Navigation Command for jumping to the next/previous clickable element in browse mode.

The magnifier command is thanks to Cyrille, and the clickable one thanks to Cary. Thank you to them and ALL of our amazing NVDA community contributors!

One of the fixes in NVDA 2026.3.1 is with reporting switching Windows in Windows 10. I was thinking of writing a post on using alt+tab and the other ways of switching Windows – there are a few! But I realised, I already wrote a piece on switching Windows .

I’d forgotten about alt+escape ; I’m going to get back into using that! But that got me thinking about other general Windows keystrokes we might not know or (like me) might have forgotten. Another recent fix in NVDA (from NVDA 2026.3) is with File Explorer, so I thought we’d have a look at a couple of shortcuts which are well worth knowing, and some you may find useful:

Firstly, to start File Explorer, press Windows+e Open a new File Explorer window (from within File Explorer), with control+n

Navigating Move to next area: tab Move to previous area: shift+tab The focus starts in the “Items view list” – the contents of the currently selected folder. From here: Press shift+tab once to the folder list (you had to press it twice in some versions). Press tab to the “Split button” which is the name of the field the item list is sorted on. Once on the split button, use the arrows to select a field and enter or space to sort on it – if you select the same field, it will reverse the sort).

When in the items list view, you can customise the view. Windows provides shortcuts for the various views: control+shift+1 : Extra-large icons control+shift+2 : Large icons control+shift+3 : Medium icons control+shift+4 : Small icons control+shift+5 : List view control+shift+6 : Details view control+shift+7 : Tiles control+shift+8 : Content Note that in some versions of Windows (such as recent builds of Windows 11) these shortcuts do NOT work, but control+ALT+number works, for instance control+alt+6 for details view. The “details” view is the one I would personally recommend, as everything is in one list, and you get the most information about each item (file type, size, date modified etc) and can sort on any of those fields as needed. In details view, use the up and down arrow keys to move through the list. In most other view types, e.g. the icons views, use the left and right arrow keys .

Tabs Like browsers, you can have multiple folders open in different tabs or different windows: New blank tab: control+t Move to next tab: control+tab Move to previous tab: control+shift+tab

I cannot find a keystroke to open the current folder in a new tab. If you know one, please let me know! In the meantime, the following would work: Press shift+f6 once from the folder list to move to the tab control list. Press the applications key (or shift+f10 ) to open the context menu. Press the up arrow once to “Duplicate tab”. Press enter to open a new tab with the current folder.

To close a tab without closing all the other tabs, press control+w .

Address bar Move the focus to the address bar: alt+d . On the address bar, you can type the name of the folder or paste it from elsewhere, then press enter to load that folder.

Windows has several special folders. If you email us for help with an issue, we might ask you to send us your NVDA log, which you can find in your %temp% folder. To get to your %temp% folder: In File Explorer, press alt+d to go to the address bar Type: %temp% (That is, the word ‘temp’ with a percent sign either side) Press enter Windows will load a folder such as C:\Users\YourName\AppData\Local\Temp which is where it is storing your temporary files. There are others such as %onedrive% for your OneDrive folder (if setup), as well as system folders which are worth being careful around.

File properties One other quirk in File Explorer is opening file properties. In the file list, once you have located a file, press alt+enter to open the file properties for that file. This only works from the file list, even though you can access “ Properties ” in the context menu on folders in the folder list and it notes the alt+enter shortcut.

That’s all for this fortnight. We’ll be back towards the end of the month with more news, tips and tricks. I’m not sure what will be in that edition, but after all those lists of things in the file manager section, I’m going to aim for zero lists next fortnight – keep an eye out for that to see if I can do it!

Do keep the conversation going in the NVDA users email group , and remember, if you’d like to receive this blog by email, you can! Just go to https://www.nvaccess.org/newsletter and you can sign up for the blog, for details as new versions of NVDA drop, and more.

en.title: Navia: AI Accessible Map
en.summary: Navia is a touchable offline map for blind and low-vision people. Slide a finger across the screen and Navia speaks the street, shop, or place…
en.body:
Published 12 November 2026 by Mohammad

Navia is a touchable offline map for blind and low-vision people. Slide a finger across the screen and Navia speaks the street, shop, or place under your finger: its name, what it is, how far away it is, and directions as clock positions (for example, “2 o’clock, 40 meters”), following the way O&M training teaches. Sweeping around the map lets you build a mental picture of an area before you go there.

Safety note: Navia is an extra aid only. Always use a cane, guide dog, or another safe mobility method first.

Free or paid:

Accessibility and User Comments:

I am the developer. Navia was designed around TalkBack from the start rather than adapted afterwards. All buttons and controls are labelled and every dialog can be read with TalkBack.

The map itself is explored by touch: with TalkBack on, sliding a finger over the map speaks what is under it, and double-tap opens a menu of actions for that place (aim, hear its sounds, open in Google Maps, add to favourites). Voice dictation is available for search, adding points and renaming places.

For low vision there is an optional drawn map with a different marker shape per kind of place (not colour alone), street labels and a light/dark theme; it can turn itself off while TalkBack is running. Tested with Google TalkBack, including automated tests that run with real TalkBack enabled.

Known limitations: AI place recognition is experimental, needs a one-time ~240 MB model download and can miss a place; map quality depends on OpenStreetMap coverage in your area. Feedback is very welcome.

Last Tested App version and Android version:

Navia 1.1.12. Android 15

No accessibility ratings yet. Be the first to rate this app.

Please use this rating only for accessibility. For feedback about the app’s features, price, overall quality, or your general experience, use the comments section below.

Please log in to rate this app’s accessibility.

es.title: Una retina artificial convierte la luz infrarroja en señales eléctricas para estimular las neuronas del ojo
es.summary: Una investigación publicada en Nature Electronics presenta un implante retiniano capaz de transformar la luz infrarroja cercana en impulsos eléctricos. El dispositivo ha conseguido generar respuestas neuronales en ratones con degeneración de la retina y abre nuevas posibilidades para el desarrollo de prótesis visuales. La ingeniería biomédica continúa explorando nuevas formas de recuperar parcialmente la […] La entrada Una retina artificial convierte la luz infrarroja en señales eléctricas para estimular las neuronas del ojo se publicó primero en Conticgo .
es.body:
Una investigación publicada en Nature Electronics presenta un implante retiniano capaz de transformar la luz infrarroja cercana en impulsos eléctricos. El dispositivo ha conseguido generar respuestas neuronales en ratones con degeneración de la retina y abre nuevas posibilidades para el desarrollo de prótesis visuales.

La ingeniería biomédica continúa explorando nuevas formas de recuperar parcialmente la percepción visual en personas con enfermedades degenerativas de la retina. Una de las últimas investigaciones en este campo propone una solución basada en una retina artificial capaz de transformar la luz infrarroja cercana en señales eléctricas que estimulan directamente las neuronas del ojo.

El trabajo, publicado en abril de 2026 en la revista científica Nature Electronics , ha sido desarrollado por investigadores de distintas instituciones de Corea del Sur. Su propuesta combina sensores fotosensibles, microelectrodos de metal líquido y un sistema electrónico implantable que permite activar determinadas células de la retina.

Los experimentos realizados en ratones, incluidos animales con degeneración retiniana, han demostrado que el dispositivo puede provocar respuestas neuronales ante estímulos de luz infrarroja.

La visión natural comienza cuando los fotorreceptores de la retina, conocidos como conos y bastones, detectan la luz y la transforman en señales eléctricas. Estas señales se procesan en diferentes capas retinianas y posteriormente se transmiten al cerebro a través del nervio óptico.

Sin embargo, enfermedades como la retinosis pigmentaria provocan la degeneración progresiva de los fotorreceptores. Aunque estas células pueden llegar a desaparecer, otras estructuras de la retina, como las células ganglionares, pueden conservar parte de su funcionalidad.

La nueva tecnología pretende aprovechar precisamente esta capacidad.

El implante incorpora una matriz de fototransistores sensibles a la luz infrarroja cercana. Estos pequeños componentes detectan la radiación y generan una respuesta eléctrica que se transmite a través de unos microelectrodos situados en contacto con las neuronas retinianas.

De esta manera, el dispositivo evita depender de los fotorreceptores dañados y utiliza una vía alternativa para transmitir información visual al cerebro.

Uno de los aspectos más innovadores de esta investigación es el material empleado para fabricar los electrodos.

Los investigadores han desarrollado unos pequeños pilares tridimensionales de metal líquido, elaborados a partir de una aleación de galio e indio. Su estructura flexible permite adaptarse mejor a la superficie irregular de la retina y establecer un contacto más cercano con las células ganglionares.

Esta característica es importante porque los electrodos rígidos convencionales pueden generar problemas cuando se implantan en tejidos biológicos tan delicados.

Además, los extremos de estos microelectrodos incorporan nanopartículas de platino que mejoran la transmisión de carga eléctrica y facilitan la estimulación neuronal.

El dispositivo también incluye un filtro óptico ultrafino, de aproximadamente 360 nanómetros de grosor, diseñado para permitir el paso de determinadas longitudes de onda infrarrojas y controlar la entrada de luz visible en los sensores.

Para comprobar el funcionamiento de esta retina artificial, el equipo realizó diferentes experimentos tanto en tejidos retinianos aislados como en animales vivos.

Las pruebas incluyeron ratones sanos y ratones con degeneración retiniana, utilizados como modelo experimental de ceguera asociada a la pérdida de fotorreceptores.

Los investigadores observaron que, cuando el dispositivo recibía luz infrarroja cercana, los fototransistores generaban impulsos eléctricos capaces de activar las células ganglionares.

Además, mediante registros de actividad cerebral y pruebas de comportamiento, comprobaron que los estímulos llegaban hasta la corteza visual de los animales.

Uno de los resultados más relevantes fue que los ratones con degeneración retiniana también mostraron respuestas ante la estimulación infrarroja. Esto indica que el sistema puede aprovechar determinadas neuronas que permanecen funcionales incluso cuando los fotorreceptores han sufrido un deterioro importante.

Los estudios de biocompatibilidad también mostraron resultados iniciales favorables. En los animales evaluados durante seis meses no se observaron signos relevantes de inflamación o deterioro del tejido asociados al implante.

La investigación podría abrir una nueva vía para desarrollar prótesis visuales destinadas a personas que han perdido los fotorreceptores como consecuencia de enfermedades degenerativas de la retina.

En patologías como la retinosis pigmentaria, la pérdida progresiva de conos y bastones puede provocar una reducción importante de la visión e incluso llegar a causar ceguera.

Sin embargo, las células ganglionares y otras neuronas internas pueden permanecer relativamente conservadas durante determinadas fases de la enfermedad.

La propuesta de los investigadores consiste en aprovechar esas estructuras para transmitir información mediante estimulación eléctrica, sin depender de los fotorreceptores originales.

Otro aspecto interesante es que el dispositivo trabaja con luz infrarroja cercana, una región del espectro electromagnético que el ojo humano no puede percibir de forma natural. Esto permitiría crear un canal artificial de percepción que complemente la visión visible que todavía conserve la persona.

Los investigadores también plantean que esta tecnología podría adaptarse en el futuro para detectar otras longitudes de onda, aunque todavía es necesario estudiar sus posibilidades.

A pesar de los resultados obtenidos, esta retina artificial todavía se encuentra en una fase experimental.

Los ensayos se han realizado en ratones y no existen resultados que permitan afirmar que el dispositivo pueda utilizarse ya en personas con retinosis pigmentaria u otras enfermedades degenerativas.

Antes de plantear su aplicación clínica será necesario estudiar su seguridad a largo plazo, mejorar su miniaturización, reducir el consumo energético y comprobar su estabilidad después de periodos prolongados de implantación.

También será fundamental investigar cómo se traduce la estimulación eléctrica en una percepción visual útil para las personas. Activar las neuronas retinianas no significa recuperar automáticamente una visión natural.

No obstante, el trabajo publicado en Nature Electronics representa un avance relevante en el desarrollo de prótesis visuales y demuestra cómo la combinación de microelectrónica y materiales biocompatibles puede abrir nuevas posibilidades para intervenir sobre el sistema visual.

en.title: Clicklet
en.summary: Clicklet lets the Camera Control button on your iPhone start your Apple Shortcuts. Pick one shortcut to launch with a press, or turn on Menu mode and choose from a few favorites each time. Clicklet opens Apple Shortcuts to run your workflow, so you'll see the usual Shortcuts screens, along with any permission prompts or app handoffs your shortcut needs. To set up your library, install the included Connect Clicklet helper. It brings in your shortcut names and small icon images, which appear in your library, in the menu, and while a shortcut opens. You can also search for a shortcut or type its name. If you used an earlier version, replace the old helper with the new one and refresh to get icons. From the menu, tap Configure to go back to setup. You can scroll the menu by dragging along its side margins. Your shortcut names, icons and selections stay on your device. There's no account, advertising, analytics, subscription or in-app purchase. Camera access supports the Camera Control and lock-screen handoff and shows a live preview; Clicklet doesn't save photos or videos. Launching while your iPhone is locked requires authentication. Requires iOS 18 or later and Apple's Shortcuts app. Launching from the button requires an iPhone with Camera Control; set Clicklet in Settings > Camera > Camera Control. Opening Clicklet on its own shows your setup without running a shortcut.

en.summary: Sight Buddy is a free, open-source Android app for asking questions about images and text. Once the models are downloaded, it works offline with no…
en.body:
Published 11 November 2026 by Tommi Drophouse

Sight Buddy is a free, open-source Android app for asking questions about images and text. Once the models are downloaded, it works offline with no account, subscription, or usage limit.

It can chat about images and text, find the right page in a document, and share, save, or copy text. The app recommends a model setup that fits the phone, so users do not need technical knowledge.

It is a new release with early users internationally, and user feedback has helped shape the design.

Source code: https://github.com/DrophouseLtd/SightBuddy

Free or paid:

Accessibility and User Comments:

In previous versions, there were some inconveniences with TalkBack labels and navigation, but these have already been fixed. All feedback is always welcome.

2.4.3. Android 17

en.title: Apple TV introduces new Sign Language interpretation feature
en.summary: Today, Apple announced a new accessibility feature on the Apple TV app offering sign language interpretation for supported titles.
en.body:
Text of this article

November 10, 2026

UPDATE

Apple TV introduces new Sign Language interpretation feature

New accessibility feature debuts Friday, November 13, with the streaming premiere of Being Heumann

Today, Apple announced a new accessibility feature for the Apple TV app that gives viewers the option to watch supported titles with accompanying sign language interpretation. 1 The feature will be available on Friday, November 13, alongside the global streaming premiere of Being Heumann , a film based on the true story of disability rights activist Judy Heumann, on Apple TV.

In addition to Being Heumann, interpretation for American Sign Language (ASL) and British Sign Language (BSL) will be available for the movie F1. Later this year, Way of the Warrior Kid and Greyhound will follow, with more Apple Original titles to come. When turned on in Apple TV app settings, the Sign Language option will appear on supported Apple Original titles.

“At Apple, we believe everyone should be able to enjoy great stories and entertainment,” said Sarah Herrlinger, Apple’s senior director of Global Accessibility Policy and Initiatives. “Bringing sign language interpretation to Apple TV is an exciting step forward in making the viewing experience more accessible and inclusive for Deaf audiences. Accessibility is a core value at Apple, and we’re proud to continue creating experiences that allow more people to enjoy the content they love.”

Designed with Native Signers in the Deaf Community

Apple TV offers a sign language experience that’s designed and tested by Deaf and native signers. Each performance is carefully crafted to fit and complement the Apple Original film it interprets.

“It’s incredibly meaningful to see our beautiful language authentically represented onscreen,” said Daniel Durant, who appears in Being Heumann and directed the film’s sign language interpretation. “Bringing this experience to life required a lot of care to ensure every translation captured the emotion and meaning of the story. I’m proud to have been part of Being Heumann and thrilled to see Apple TV supporting greater accessibility for Deaf audiences.”

New Ways to Discover Titles with Sign Language

Titles with sign language interpretation will be labeled with a Sign Language icon, making it easy to know when the option is available. Viewers can enable the feature in Apple TV app settings, then press the Sign Language button while watching. Search will also make it easier to find titles that feature sign language with simple phrases like “with ASL.”

As sign language interpretation becomes more widely available across streaming services, the new “Movies & Shows with American Sign Language” collection on the Apple TV app will offer viewers a simple way to explore titles featuring sign language, in one dedicated destination.

Being Heumann

In Being Heumann , Judy Heumann (Ruth Madeley) — scrappy, defiant, and done being treated like a burden — turns her outrage into a revolution. In San Francisco in 1977, she and more than 100 disability rights protesters organize a sit-in to send a very loud message: The system is broken — not us. The film marks the second collaboration between Apple Original Films and writer-director Siân Heder, who directed the multi-Academy Award-winning film CODA, which made history as the first film with a predominantly Deaf cast to receive the Best Picture honor.

Being Heumann premieres globally on Apple TV on Friday, November 13. Viewers can add Being Heumann to their watchlist on Apple TV .

Apple TV offers premium, compelling drama and comedy series, feature films, groundbreaking documentaries, and kids and family entertainment, and is available to watch across all of a user’s favorite screens. After its launch on November 1, 2019, Apple TV became the first all-original streaming service to launch around the world, and has premiered more original hits and received more award recognitions faster than any other streaming service in its debut. To date, Apple Original films, documentaries, and series have been honored with 919 wins and 3,829 award nominations and counting, including Academy Award Best Picture winner CODA and Academy Award winner F1, the highest-grossing sports feature of all time.

About Apple TV

Apple TV is available on the Apple TV app in 170 countries and regions, on over 1 billion screens, including iPhone; iPad; Apple TV 4K; Apple Vision Pro; Mac; popular smart TVs from Samsung, LG, Sony, VIZIO, TCL, and others; Roku and Amazon Fire TV devices; Chromecast with Google TV; PlayStation and Xbox gaming consoles; and at tv.apple.com , for $14.99 per month with a seven-day free trial for new subscribers. For a limited time, customers who purchase and activate a new iPhone, iPad, Apple TV 4K, or Mac can enjoy three months of Apple TV for free. 2

For more information, visit apple.com/tvpr and see the full list of supported devices .
