es.title: Cadence Tactile Tablet, la pantalla táctil que permite explorar gráficos, braille y vídeo en tiempo real
es.summary: El acceso a la información digital sigue planteando importantes barreras para las personas ciegas y con discapacidad visual. Aunque las líneas braille y los lectores de pantalla han facilitado considerablemente el uso de ordenadores y dispositivos electrónicos, determinados contenidos, como gráficos, mapas, imágenes o vídeos, continúan siendo difíciles de explorar de forma autónoma. En este […] La entrada Cadence Tactile Tablet, la pantalla táctil que permite explorar gráficos, braille y vídeo en tiempo real se publicó primero en Conticgo .
es.body:
El acceso a la información digital sigue planteando importantes barreras para las personas ciegas y con discapacidad visual. Aunque las líneas braille y los lectores de pantalla han facilitado considerablemente el uso de ordenadores y dispositivos electrónicos, determinados contenidos, como gráficos, mapas, imágenes o vídeos, continúan siendo difíciles de explorar de forma autónoma.

En este contexto surge Cadence Tactile Tablet , un dispositivo desarrollado por la empresa estadounidense Tactile Engineering que propone una nueva forma de interactuar con los contenidos digitales: una pantalla táctil dinámica capaz de representar texto en braille, gráficos e incluso imágenes en movimiento.

A diferencia de las líneas braille tradicionales, que presentan los caracteres de forma secuencial en una única línea, Cadence incorpora una superficie formada por pequeños puntos móviles que pueden elevarse y descender para representar información mediante el tacto.

Su pantalla dispone de 384 puntos táctiles , distribuidos en 48 celdas braille de ocho puntos, organizadas en cuatro líneas de doce celdas. Esta configuración permite consultar varias líneas de texto simultáneamente y explorar representaciones gráficas sin depender exclusivamente de descripciones verbales.

El dispositivo utiliza tecnología MEMS ( Micro-Electro-Mechanical Systems ), basada en sistemas microelectromecánicos, para controlar el movimiento de los puntos táctiles. Según el fabricante, estos pueden actualizarse hasta tres veces por segundo, permitiendo modificar la información que aparece bajo los dedos.

Una de las características más llamativas de Cadence es su capacidad para representar gráficos táctiles dinámicos. Esto significa que la superficie no se limita a mostrar una imagen estática, sino que puede modificar los puntos en tiempo real para transmitir información cambiante.

Entre sus posibilidades destacan:

Una demostración especialmente llamativa tuvo lugar durante las 500 Millas de Indianápolis de 2026. Mediante Cadence, los aficionados ciegos pudieron seguir táctilmente el movimiento de los coches en el circuito, convirtiendo la información visual de la carrera en patrones que cambiaban bajo sus dedos.

Esta experiencia muestra cómo la tecnología táctil puede ampliar el acceso no solo a la lectura y al aprendizaje, sino también a acontecimientos deportivos y contenidos audiovisuales.

Otra de sus particularidades es su diseño modular. Cadence puede utilizarse como una unidad independiente o conectarse con otras unidades para ampliar la superficie táctil disponible.

El fabricante contempla configuraciones de hasta cuatro dispositivos conectados, que permiten trabajar con una superficie de mayor tamaño y representar contenidos más amplios.

Además, incorpora teclado braille tipo Perkins, controles direccionales y botones multifunción para navegar por los contenidos, seleccionar líneas, acceder a etiquetas y controlar diferentes aplicaciones.

La conexión con ordenadores y dispositivos compatibles se realiza mediante Bluetooth o USB-C. También dispone de software propio, CadenceOS, que permite gestionar el dispositivo y acceder a diferentes aplicaciones y contenidos.

Las aplicaciones de una pantalla táctil de estas características pueden ser especialmente interesantes en el ámbito educativo.

El acceso a mapas, gráficos matemáticos, representaciones científicas y otros recursos visuales constituye uno de los grandes retos de la educación inclusiva. Aunque existen materiales en relieve y herramientas de adaptación, su elaboración puede requerir tiempo, conocimientos especializados y recursos específicos.

Dispositivos como Cadence permiten explorar nuevas formas de presentar estos contenidos digitalmente, facilitando su actualización y ofreciendo posibilidades de interacción que no proporcionan los materiales táctiles estáticos.

También pueden contribuir al acceso a información que cambia constantemente, como gráficos estadísticos, retransmisiones deportivas o determinadas representaciones audiovisuales.

No obstante, es importante recordar que la disponibilidad de una pantalla táctil dinámica no garantiza por sí sola la accesibilidad de cualquier contenido. La distribución de los puntos, la complejidad de las representaciones y la necesidad de una adaptación comprensible siguen siendo aspectos fundamentales para que la información pueda interpretarse correctamente mediante el tacto.

Cadence Tactile Tablet representa una evolución interesante dentro de la tiflotecnología: pasar de dispositivos centrados principalmente en reproducir texto braille a superficies capaces de transmitir información espacial y dinámica.

Su desarrollo abre nuevas posibilidades para la lectura, la educación, la comunicación y el acceso a contenidos digitales. También plantea una cuestión importante de cara al futuro: cómo conseguir que las imágenes, los gráficos y otros contenidos diseñados originalmente para la vista puedan convertirse en experiencias táctiles realmente comprensibles y accesibles.

La tecnología todavía tiene retos por delante, pero propuestas como esta muestran que el futuro de la accesibilidad digital también pasa por ampliar las posibilidades del sentido del tacto.

Si te ha gustado esta noticia no te pierdas las últimas novedades en tiflotectnología en nuestro apartado de noticias y redes sociales .

en.title: NoteTell Money Reader
en.summary: NoteTell Money Reader is designed to help people who are blind or have low vision identify bills in real time. Simply point the iPhone camera at the bill you want to identify, then hear, feel, or see its value. If you’re blind, have low vision, or are deafblind, NoteTell Money Reader lets you identify bills without any assistance. While shopping, use NoteTell to check your money at the checkout and make sure you get the right change back. You can also use NoteTell to quickly sort your money at home. NoteTell doesn’t require an internet connection, so it identifies bills anywhere, at any time. NoteTell can identify bills at any angle. It is designed to work with bills that are folded, creased, worn, or partly in view. NoteTell is designed to work indoors, outdoors, and even in total darkness. When your environment is too dark to identify bills, NoteTell turns the flashlight on automatically. Vibration Mode tells you the value of each bill as vibrations in your hand—without anyone else hearing it. Each bill has its own vibration pattern. The lowest bill has one pulse, and each higher bill has one more. Pulses come in pairs, so they’re easier to count. Vibration Mode is also useful in noisy places and for people who are deafblind. When VoiceOver is on, double-tap with two fingers to switch between Speech Mode and Vibration Mode. For users with low vision, NoteTell shows the value of each bill in large, high-contrast numbers on the screen. You can complete every task in NoteTell Money Reader using only VoiceOver, without sighted assistance. If you use a braille display with VoiceOver, you can use NoteTell to get the value of each bill in real time. Ask Siri, “Identify currency with NoteTell,” to use NoteTell hands-free. You can also add NoteTell to Control Center or the Lock Screen, assign it to the Action button, or set it up as a Vocal Shortcut. With the full version, you can use Currency Conversion to hear each bill’s value in your home currency when you travel. NoteTell uses on-device processing to identify bills, which means your data never leaves your iPhone. Camera images are never stored on the device or on any servers. You can try the full version free for 14 days. You won’t be charged when the trial ends. You can continue using NoteTell for free to identify the lowest notes of each currency. The full version is also available as a one-time purchase. And with Family Sharing, up to five other people can enjoy your purchase too.

en.title: Apple Releases Version 27.2.1 of iOS, iPadOS, macOS, and watchOS with Bug Fixes and Security Updates
en.summary: Apple has today released version 27.2.1 of iOS, iPadOS, macOS, and watchOS, bringing bug fixes and security updates, including for a vulnerability that allowed macOS command line tools to use compromised eMudhra certificates. As the 27.2.1 updates were not distributed to external testers prior to their release, we do not have any information on whether they contain any accessibility fixes for blind, deaf blind, or low vision users at the time of writing. However, as these updates appear to have been released to address a small number of specific issues, we do not expect them to contain any such fixes. Release Notes iOS 27.2.1 This update provides bug fixes and security updates for your iPhone. For information on the security content of Apple software updates, please visit: https://support.apple.com/100100 . iPadOS 27.2.1 This update provides bug fixes and security updates for your iPad. For information on the security content of Apple software updates, please visit: https://support.apple.com/100100 . macOS Golden Gate 27.2.1 This update provides bug fixes and security updates for your Mac. watchOS 27.2.1 This update provides bug fixes and security updates for your Apple Watch. For information on the security content of Apple software updates, please visit: https://support.apple.com/100100 . How to Update iOS and iPadOS 27.2.1 are available over-the-air (Settings > General > Software Update), via Finder on a Mac with macOS Catalina or later, or via iTunes on a PC or Mac with macOS Mojave or earlier. Before updating, we strongly recommend making a full and complete backup of your device (either locally or in iCloud, depending on personal preference). This will ensure that, in the unlikely event that something goes wrong during the update process, you will have a current backup on hand in case a device restore becomes necessary. Also, if updating OTA, we recommend plugging your device into a power source for the duration of the download/installation process, so as to prevent the unlikely event of your battery going dead during the update. To install macOS Golden Gate 27.2.1, choose System Settings from the Apple menu, select General in the table, click Software Update in the scroll area, and click the Update Now button to begin the update process. If other updates are available, you can click the Info button to see details about them and select specific updates to install. watchOS 27.2.1 is available over-the-air (Settings > General > Software Update) or by going to the Watch app on your iPhone and navigating to General > Software Update. To install the update, your Watch must be connected to its charger and have at least 50% battery power.

es.summary: Normal 0 false 21 false false false ES X-NONE X-NONE /* Style Definitions */ table.MsoNormalTable {mso-style-name:"Tabla normal"; mso-tstyle-rowband-size:0; mso-tstyle-colband-size:0; mso-style-noshow:yes; mso-style-priority:99; mso-style-parent:""; mso-padding-alt:0cm 5.4pt 0cm 5.4pt; mso-para-margin-top:0cm; mso-para-margin-right:0cm; mso-para-margin-bottom:8.0pt; mso-para-margin-left:0cm; line-height:107%; mso-pagination:widow-orphan; font-size:11.0pt; font-family:"Calibri",sans-serif; mso-ascii-font-family:Calibri; mso-ascii-theme-font:minor-latin; mso-hansi-font-family:Calibri; mso-hansi-theme-font:minor-latin; mso-bidi-font-family:"Times New Roman"; mso-bidi-theme-font:minor-bidi; mso-fareast-language:EN-US;} Hola gente, ¿qué tal les va? Después de bastante tiempo trabajando en un proyecto nuevo y distinto dentro de la familia TCA Software, ¡por fin llega TCA DjMix 1.0! ¿Pero qué es TCA DjMix? Si eres de los que creció viendo a algún DJ mezclar pistas con fundidos suaves y sincronizando beats al milisegundo… pues este es tu programa. Y lo mejor: está diseñado desde cero para que cualquiera pueda usarlo con lector de pantalla. Sí, lo has leído bien. TCA DjMix es la primera aplicación de DJ accesible para Windows pensada específicamente para quienes usamos NVDA, JAWS o Narrador. Pero no es solo para nosotros: cualquier persona puede usarla con teclado, con ratón o incluso con una controladora MIDI. Y esto tiene algo todavía más especial: este es el primer programa de toda la familia TCA Software que fue construido usando Inteligencia Artificial. Sí, justo como lo lees. Por primera vez en la historia de TCA Software, creamos un programa "by coding" con ayuda de IA. CARACTERÍSTICAS PRINCIPALES TCA DjMix es una aplicación de mezcla musical accesible que reúne todo lo necesario para crear tus sesiones. Estas son sus funciones clave: • Biblioteca unificada y platos independientes TCA DjMix incluye una biblioteca centralizada donde cargas tu carpeta de música, la cual se navega 100% con lector de pantalla y lista todos los archivos automáticamente (formatos compatibles: WAV, FLAC, OGG, MP3 y AIFF). Desde esa misma lista puedes cargar las pistas de manera independiente en el plato 1 o en el plato 2 usando los atajos (Alt+1 o Alt+2), controlando el volumen y la reproducción de cada plato por separado. • Sincronización automática de BPM (Beatmatch) El Beatmatch automático analiza ambas pistas y ajusta sus tempos para que se sincronicen solos. Ideal para quienes están empezando y no quieren complicarse ajustando a mano. • Crossfader accesible El crossfader permite hacer fundidos suaves entre los dos platos, tal como lo hacen los DJ profesionales. Se puede controlar cómodamente desde el teclado o con el ratón. • Efectos de sonido (Samples) Puedes agregar efectos como scratches, fades o hits con un solo atajo de teclado. Solo hay que poner los archivos WAV de efectos en la carpeta "samples" y ya están listos para sonar. • Compatible con controladoras MIDI (funcionalidad en versión prueba). Si tienes una controladora Pioneer DDJ-400, DDJ-SR o DDJ-SR2, TCA DjMix la detecta automáticamente. No hace falta configurar nada: conéctala y empieza a mezclar usando los controles físicos que ya conoces. Atajos de teclado útiles Algunos de los atajos más prácticos para controlar todo con el teclado: • Ctrl+L: Abrir carpeta y cargar música en la biblioteca. • Alt+1 / Alt+2: Cargar pista seleccionada en el plato 1 o plato 2. • F5 / F6: Reproducir o pausar el plato 1 / plato 2. • F7 / F8: Detener el plato 1 / plato 2. • Tab: Recorrer controles. • Ctrl+B: Sincronizar el plato activo con el otro plato. • Ctrl+F1 a Ctrl+F12: Reproducir samples del banco actual. • Ctrl+S: Detener todos los samples. • Ctrl+M: Iniciar o detener la automezcla. • Ctrl+P: Abrir la configuración. • Ctrl+J: Panel de controladora MIDI. ¿QUIÉN PUEDE USARLO? TCA DjMix está pensado para cualquier persona interesada en la mezcla musical, pero especialmente para personas ciegas o con baja visión que usan lectores de pantalla y que siempre soñaron con hacer una mezcla como un DJ profesional. Con los atajos correctos y un poco de práctica, cualquiera puede manejarlo sin necesidad de ver la pantalla. Y hablando de práctica... ¡te lo ponemos muy fácil! Más abajo, en esta misma entrada, te dejamos el tutorial en audio y vídeo donde puedes ver y escuchar el programa en acción paso a paso. Compatibilidad de TCA DjMix 1.0: El programa es compatible con: • Windows 10 X64. • Windows 11. • TCA DjMix 1.0 se distribuye como un archivo ZIP descargable. Incluye todo lo necesario: el ejecutable, los samples predeterminados y las instrucciones. No requiere instalación, simplemente descomprime y ejecuta. • Es multilenguaje: español, italiano, inglés y portugués. • En algunos PC, podrían necesitar la instalación de las librerías Visual Estudio C++ (en la descarga estarán). La descarga. Les dejaré en la descarga: • El audio tutorial (en los canales Odysse y YouTube estará en video tutorial). • El programa: TCA DjMix 1.0. • Archivo con las librerías Visual Estudio C++. TCA DjMix es una herramienta que demuestra que la accesibilidad en la tecnología musical no tiene por qué ser un sueño imposible. Con un diseño pensado desde cero para lectores de pantalla, soporte para controladoras MIDI reales y funciones profesionales como beatmatch automático y efectos de sonido, este programa abre las puertas del mundo DJ a personas que antes tenían dificultades para acceder a estas herramientas. Y lo más bonito: nació del esfuerzo dentro de la familia TCA Software, que ahora además cuenta con IA como herramienta de desarrollo. ¿Quién dice que no se puede? ¡Los leo en los comentarios! es.summary: Tras una candidata a liberación, NV Access ha anunciado mediante esta publicación que ya se encuentra disponible para su descarga la versión final de NVDA 2026.3.1, el lector de pantalla gratuito y de código abierto para Microsoft Windows. Se recomienda a todos los usuarios actualizar a esta nueva versión, cuyo uso se considera apto también … Continuar leyendo "Ya disponible la versión final de NVDA 2026.3.1 con correcciones de seguridad" La entrada Ya disponible la versión final de NVDA 2026.3.1 con correcciones de seguridad se publicó primero en NVDA en español .
es.body:
Tras una candidata a liberación, NV Access ha anunciado mediante esta publicación que ya se encuentra disponible para su descarga la versión final de NVDA 2026.3.1, el lector de pantalla gratuito y de código abierto para Microsoft Windows. Se recomienda a todos los usuarios actualizar a esta nueva versión, cuyo uso se considera apto también en entornos de producción.

Esta versión contiene un parche que resuelve incidencias de seguridad. También corrige un fallo introducido en NVDA 2026.3 con el conmutador de tareas de Windows 10. Se ha restaurado la voz de Espeak NG en portugués de Brasil al comportamiento que tenía en NVDA 2026.2. Tan pronto como actualices NVDA, no olvides reiniciar el equipo. El reinicio garantiza que se pueden actualizar archivos que antes no se podían modificar porque estaban abiertos para escritura. En la práctica, al reiniciar vuelven a funcionar aplicaciones basadas en Electron, tales como Teams, Dropbox o Google Drive, y dejan de producirse comportamientos extraños con el explorador de archivos, Thunderbird, Office y algunos navegadores. Reiniciar es lo primero que debes hacer antes de informar de cualquier fallo. Hazlo pulsando windows+d para ir al escritorio, alt+f4, e intro sobre la opción Reiniciar. Puedes descargar NVDA 2026.3, así como las últimas versiones compatibles con sistemas antiguos y material útil para desarrolladores, desde nuestra página de descargas . La suma SHA256 de NVDA 2026.3.1, que se usa para garantizar la integridad de la descarga, es 6f80a5b0ca720a7d0d314b5be212f37388bbe81a1107ac3298c1821a1cd3f052. Si tienes una versión estable anterior, también puedes actualizar automáticamente desde el menú Ayuda. Y desde la rc1, con el complemento Selector del canal de actualización, se puede hacer del mismo modo configurando previamente el canal estable. Si todavía no conoces NVDA y quieres leer algo más sobre él antes de probarlo, te recomendamos consultar la guía de usuario y la referencia rápida de órdenes . Si te gustan nuestros proyectos y el contenido que ofrecemos, plantéate contribuir mensualmente con una pequeña cantidad. Tan sólo un euro es capaz de marcar la diferencia y ayudarnos a mejorar. Visita la página de donaciones para obtener más información, o la tienda para hacerte con libros de formación traducidos y sintetizadores de voz de alta calidad. ¡Feliz lunes!

en.title: How To Route Screen Reader Audio To Different Devices With Sandfly Screen Reader
en.summary: There is no need to explain why a screen reader user might sometimes want to have the screen reader’s audio routed to a different audio…
en.body:
Published 8 November 2026 by Kareen Kiwan

There is no need to explain why a screen reader user might sometimes want to have the screen reader’s audio routed to a different audio device than the default one.

On Android, this is not natively possible. Samsung’s One UI offers a workaround through the Separate App Sound feature, which gets the job done, even if it is not perfect. However, to my knowledge, other OEMs do not offer a comparable feature.

TalkBack, Android’s default built-in screen reader, does not offer a similar capability either. Sandfly , an open-source screen reader, allows users to change the device used to output the screen reader’s speech and audio. It also provides an option to route the audio to the phone’s speaker when specific audio devices are connected.

Sandfly is not the only screen reader that provides this feature. Another screen reader that offers similar functionality is Backtalk , and other screen readers might have something similar. However, this post only covers how to use the audio output feature found in Sandfly. Note that setting up Sandfly is outside the scope of this post.

Open Sandfly settings. You can access them from the Sandfly menu or by selecting Sandfly from the list of installed accessibility services. You can also access the settings by selecting the app from the apps list.

Find “Audio output” and activate it.

Then, press “Audio output device” to see a list of currently available audio devices, including System Default, Phone Speaker, and connected wired and wireless audio devices.

Select any device to route Sandfly’s audio through it.

To have the audio come out of the phone’s speaker when a certain device is connected, choose “Phone speaker with these devices” and check all the devices you want. Whenever one of the selected devices is connected, Sandfly’s audio will come out of the phone’s speaker instead of the connected device.

Use the “Keep speech on the phone while casting” option to determine whether you want the screen reader’s audio to come out of the phone’s speaker when you cast your screen.

Although Sandfly is not my primary screen reader at the moment, I tested Audio Output and was impressed by the reliability of the audio routing. I was able to switch between Bluetooth headphones, wired USB-C earbuds, and the phone’s speakers without any issues or interference with media playback. This is consistent with tests conducted by other team members, including full-time Sandfly users.

Published in Tips and Tricks Tutorials

en.title: Evermyth - God Life Simulator
en.summary: Become a god. Rule the world. Evermyth is a mythic life sim where you play a god from your very first prayer. Choose your domain, win the faithful, build an island realm, fall in love and face the other gods. Every life is a new myth, and every choice is yours. CHOOSE 1 OF 12 DOMAINS Death, War, Love, Sea, Sky, Nature, Knowledge, Order, Chaos, Craft, Fortune or Hearth. Each plays differently, with its own powers, prayers and stories. Be born to your seat, spring from the world itself, rise from mortal life, or seize the throne from the god before you. CREATE YOUR GOD Shape your face, hair, eyes, crown and robes in hand-drawn art inspired by ancient Greek pottery. Name your cult, choose its sacred sign, and fill a pantheon of twelve with Greek, Roman or Egyptian gods, or invent your own. WIELD 400+ DIVINE POWERS Send the rain. Hurl thunder at the assembly. Curse a king. Raise the dead. Awaken five aspects of your domain and unleash great acts: drown the world in a flood, raise a golden city, or walk among mortals in disguise. ANSWER PRAYERS, SHAPE MORTAL LIVES 400+ prayers, nearly 700 events and 240+ story chains that unfold across years. Shipwrecks, secrets, plagues, weddings, prophecies and family feuds. Every choice has a price, and mortals remember what you did. FACE CALAMITY Locust years, plague ships, great fires, a waking mountain. Save your people, bargain with another god, or let the world burn. WAGE WAR Rival realms want your island. Read your scouts and fight round by round: charge, hold the line, flank, or call down your domain to turn the battle. Sack cities, take tribute or make peace. RAISE A DIVINE BEAST Dragon, kraken, leviathan, hydra, basilisk, great wolf, golden lion, shadow panther, nine-tailed fox, star stag or moon moth. Feed it, train it, fly together, and loose it on your enemies before a hero comes hunting. LOVE, SCHEME AND FEUD Flirt, feast, beguile, trade favors and hold grudges. Marry, raise godborn children, and decide which of them deserves your seat. Win the favor of every court, from the God of the Sky to the smallest river nymph. GODS CAN FALL Rivals and even your own children can challenge you to a contest to the death. Win, and end them the old ways: cast into the pit, chained beneath a mountain, torn apart or swallowed whole. Lose, and your myth may end there. BUILD YOUR REALM Raise temples, markets, harbors, theaters and a Colossus. Keep nobles, priests and commoners on your side, or rule by fear. Change your island's climate, dress your city in your colors, and watch it come alive from dawn to night. GROW YOUR FAITH Turn a handful of believers into ten thousand faithful. Found oracles, ordain a high priest and choose the doctrines of your worship. LIVE A GOD'S OWN LIFE Wander the world as yourself, a mortal or a beast. Visit the Oracle and the Fates, take up pastimes, witness rare wonders, and earn epithets like the Merciful, Godslayer or Ender of Ages. BECOME A LEGEND Pass your seat to an heir and play on as them, or rise to the sky and set yourself among the stars. Every ended myth joins your Hall of Myths. Then begin again as a new god in a new age. PLAY YOUR WAY Free to play with no time limit. Three difficulties, from Gentle to Cruel. Day, evening and night modes. Plays offline, and no accounts, ads, subscriptions, energy timers or currencies.

Choose your domain, win the faithful, build an island realm, fall in love and face the other gods. Every life is a new myth, and every choice is yours. CHOOSE 1 OF 12 DOMAINS Death, War, Love, Sea, Sky, Nature, Knowledge, Order, Chaos, Craft, Fortune or Hearth. Each plays differently, with its own powers, prayers and stories. Be born to your seat, spring from the world itself, rise from mortal life, or seize the throne from the god before you. CREATE YOUR GOD Shape your face, hair, eyes, crown and robes in hand-drawn art inspired by ancient Greek pottery. Name your cult, choose its sacred sign, and fill a pantheon of twelve with Greek, Roman or Egyptian gods, or invent your own. WIELD 400+ DIVINE POWERS Send the rain. Hurl thunder at the assembly. Curse a king. Raise the dead. Awaken five aspects of your domain and unleash great acts: drown the world in a flood, raise a golden city, or walk among mortals in disguise. ANSWER PRAYERS, SHAPE MORTAL LIVES 400+ prayers, nearly 700 events and 240+ story chains that unfold across years. Shipwrecks, secrets, plagues, weddings, prophecies and family feuds. Every choice has a price, and mortals remember what you did. FACE CALAMITY Locust years, plague ships, great fires, a waking mountain. Save your people, bargain with another god, or let the world burn. WAGE WAR Rival realms want your island. Read your scouts and fight round by round: charge, hold the line, flank, or call down your domain to turn the battle. Sack cities, take tribute or make peace. RAISE A DIVINE BEAST Dragon, kraken, leviathan, hydra, basilisk, great wolf, golden lion, shadow panther, nine-tailed fox, star stag or moon moth. Feed it, train it, fly together, and loose it on your enemies before a hero comes hunting. LOVE, SCHEME AND FEUD Flirt, feast, beguile, trade favors and hold grudges. Marry, raise godborn children, and decide which of them deserves your seat. Win the favor of every court, from the God of the Sky to the smallest river nymph. GODS CAN FALL Rivals and even your own children can challenge you to a contest to the death. Win, and end them the old ways: cast into the pit, chained beneath a mountain, torn apart or swallowed whole. Lose, and your myth may end there. BUILD YOUR REALM Raise temples, markets, harbors, theaters and a Colossus. Keep nobles, priests and commoners on your side, or rule by fear. Change your island's climate, dress your city in your colors, and watch it come alive from dawn to night. GROW YOUR FAITH Turn a handful of believers into ten thousand faithful. Found oracles, ordain a high priest and choose the doctrines of your worship. LIVE A GOD'S OWN LIFE Wander the world as yourself, a mortal or a beast. Visit the Oracle and the Fates, take up pastimes, witness rare wonders, and earn epithets like the Merciful, Godslayer or Ender of Ages. BECOME A LEGEND Pass your seat to an heir and play on as them, or rise to the sky and set yourself among the stars. Every ended myth joins your Hall of Myths. Then begin again as a new god in a new age. PLAY YOUR WAY Free to play with no time limit. Three difficulties, from Gentle to Cruel. Day, evening and night modes. Plays offline, and no accounts, ads, subscriptions, energy timers or currencies.

en.title: Corner Grocer: Market Sim
en.summary: Run a little neighborhood market. Order stock, fill the shelves, set your prices, ring up customers at the register, and grow your shop from a corner store into a premium market with a second branch. Corner Grocer is a market management game built to be played with VoiceOver from the very first day. Sighted players and VoiceOver players play the same game with the same rules. A DAY AT THE MARKET • Morning: check deliveries, prices and today's event, then place your orders in the office. • Open: customers come in, ask for help and queue up. Scan their items, take cash or card, and count out the change. • Stock: open crates in the stockroom, put goods on the right shelves and watch the dates. Goods go off, and a wrong shelf sells less. • Evening: read the report, get one clear tip for tomorrow and decide what to invest in. GROW • Start with an empty corner shop and a basket of bread. Earn, then invest: shelves, fridges, freezers, produce stands, bakery cases and deli counters in build mode. • Move up through four store sizes: corner shop, mini market, big market and premium market. • License new product lines. There are 48 products, from bread and milk to hummus, pet food and olive oil. • Open extra registers and hire cashiers. Your own register is always yours. • Much later, open a second branch run by a manager you choose, and read its result in the evening report. • Invest in upgrades, supplier contracts and campaigns. Contracts and campaigns can renew themselves. • In the office, one button fills your order from the suggestions. In the stockroom, one button places every crate that has room. • Daily goals, 22 achievements, and events such as heat waves, rain, power cuts, rival sales and supplier delays. • There is no final day. Play as long as you like. BUILT FOR VOICEOVER • Every station has labelled controls in a fixed order, plus actions for the rotor. Anything you can drag also has a way to do without dragging. • Three speech levels: Full, Balanced and Sounds First. • Magic Tap pauses and resumes the day. • Sound carries information: door chimes, scanner beeps, queue alerts, shelf warnings. The Listening Room in Settings plays every sound and tells you what it means. • Easy, Normal and Custom modes, with assists for patience, day length, customer flow, wrong-shelf protection, undo and clearing spoiled goods each morning. Assists are for everyone and always free. • Short optional small jobs fill the quiet moments at the register. • Customer voices are generated with AI. You can turn them down or off in Settings. MAKE IT YOURS Decorate your shop in the Shop Studio: floors, walls, counters, signs, lights, decor and outfits, plus atmospheres, music albums and end-of-day tunes. Name your shop and let the game describe it to you. FREE TO PLAY, WITH OPTIONAL ADS AND PURCHASES The game is free to download. Cash from the shop pays for stock, shelves and upgrades. Coins are only for sound and looks; earn them by playing or with an optional ad in the Shop Studio, or buy Coin packs. Accessibility features and Easy mode are always free. ADS AND SUPPORT PACKS Ads come from Google AdMob and never play while the shop is open. From day 3 a short full-screen ad can play between days, with or without VoiceOver; the game says when an ad starts and when it closes. Once a day, an optional ad in the evening report doubles that day's profit. Support packs (Starter, Supporter, Founder) remove ads, double the evening profit without an ad and give every new shop extra starting cash. Ads are personalised only if you allow tracking. Play in 11 languages: English, Turkish, German, Spanish, French, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese (Brazil), Russian and Chinese (Simplified). Customers speak all 11 languages. English and Turkish voices come with the app; the others download once while you are online. Questions or feedback: support@birkinapps.com

en.title: The Day Bingo Went to Brent Cross, Met the iPhone Duo, and Bought a Pizza
en.summary: Introduction Dear old Brent Cross has featured quite heavily in my life. When I was a child, it was a brand spanking new shopping centre, famed for being absolutely enormous as well as the first attempt outside London to bring shopping and entertainment together. London had its west end, and we in north London had our north-west end in Brent Cross. My family, certain of whom have a worrying fixation with shopping trips, used to love it. Later in life, Brent Cross was where I went to get my wedding suit made. Note, dear gentleman readers, that I had my suit made, not hired, and and you should not allow yourselves to be wed in someone else's clothes either. After all, is the bride going to hire her wedding dress? Brent Cross is also where our Apple Store is, and last Saturday I persuaded Mrs Bingo to come along with me and meet the new iPhone line-up. Now, notwithstanding I've been to Brent Cross many times, I've never been on a Saturday afternoon. Don't! It's phenomenally busy and immediately put pay to the idea that I might capture a nice, atmospheric audio review of my iPhone explorations. Audio there is, but it is unfit for human consumption. Plus, although we've both been to the Apple Store there a couple of times, we had forgotten where it was. Cue a quarter of an hour wandering around past every chain store imaginable alongside coffee shops and a pop-up pizzeria, which admittedly we noted down as a place to visit on the way out, we finally remembered it was on the upper level and got there in in the end. It was the work of a moment to find a demo iPhone Duo model with which to play, safely cabled to the counter as a countermeasure to light-fingered iProdders. Let the games begin, as they say. What This Review is, and What it Ain't I want to kick off by setting some parameters. These are my unfiltered impressions. I'm not a tech journalist so I'll not be getting down and dirty with the processing power or what have you. I'm also assuming you're someone who either has the budget for the duo or who is at least very curious and perhaps wishes they had. So I'll be entirely subjective about whether it's worth the money—ultimately, that's a value judgement for each and every one of us. There may be a bit of repetition if you're familiar with other iPhone Duo pioneers' output, like the excellent Dave Nason's contributions, and if that happens it's purely coincidental, and a byproduct of my giving you my unfiltered impressions. But I have tried to keep this to a minimum and I also cross-refer to Dave's contribution, so please look at that if you haven't already. For you braillists out there, you'll be pleased to learn I did get a good go at BSI. Still reading? Thank gawd for that! A Jet-Setter's Passport Those who say the Duo is like a passport are not wrong. It really is more or less the same size and shape. I'm not talking a passport that most people have, however. I mean a passport like my mate Penguin has, because he is sent to so many foreign parts by his employer. In the UK, we have a choice of adding a good few extra pages to our passport if we're like Penguin. the Duo's like Penguin's passport, so a bit thicker than mine. Never mind Penguin, Bingo! How does it feel in the hand? Honestly? Fantastic. Size, weight, everything. I can't fault it. True, I couldn't test it in the pocket as I suspect various alarms would have gone off and I did not have a pocket at quite the right height what with its being cabled to the table and all that lark, but I could tell there'd be no trouble fitting it in any but the smallest of pockets. Dave Nason has commented on the weight. I have to say, I didn't find this at all noticeable. It is, perhaps, the weight of a wallet with a reasonable number of coins in it. That's what it feels like to hold. Not a wallet stuffed full to the seams, but a wallet with a handful of change in it. I say that on the assumption that anyone can still remember what carrying cash was like. Now, I admit I didn't hold it in my hand for very long, whereas Dave has actually been using one; but even allowing for that I was not at all concerned. Sure, it's heavier than an iPhone Air, but that's what you expect. Know When to Fold Up Dave has covered this in some detail already. For my part, I found the magnetic snap as the Duo folded very satisfying. The thing looks a very robust piece of kit when folded. When unfolded, in small tablet mode, it still feels solid—not unlike the 9.4in iPad Pro I used to own. Like Dave, I could feel the crease at the centre point but not unpleasantly so, and it does serve as a very handy orientation point. For me, and accidental though this benefit may be, I preferred it to the iPad because of this. Sound as a Pound I was in a very busy Apple Store, so bear that in mind. Additionally, the only settings I changed were to enable BSI's quick activation gesture. I played no music and listened to no books. Nevertheless, I thought Daniel compact sounded very good, both in folded and unfolded landscape modes. Indeed, the latter reminded me of the beautiful audio that I used to get from the iPad Pro. I would therefore conclude that Apple must be doing something right with this. Was it any better than the audio from the iPhone 18 Pro, which I also tried? In unfolded landscape, I would say it was, though if you're in the market for a Pro and you have a 16 Pro Max like I do, I would immediately agree that the 18 Pro is a big step up from that, and worth it for the audio alone. Braille Screen Input I had really wanted to try this and I was blown away. In unfolded Landscape, the Duo was a breeze for BSI in tabletop mode. I tried typing as fast as the cable on the table would allow in a blank note in the notes app and made hardly any errors. Those I did make were down to the unfortunate stoop I had to adopt owing to the cable on the table aforesaid, compounded by Voiceover's being set to speak both characters and words—I had forgotten how utterly tiresome I find that much keyboard echo and how it appears to slow one down. I then folded the phone and tried it in Screen Away Mode. All I can say is the speed of my Landscape tabletop typing was blasted out of the water. Again, I tried to braille as fast as I could and I can't remember making any errors. Indeed, an Apple Store employee (a South African gentleman who rather unconvincingly assured me he wasn't sneakily checking the rugby score between Italy and South Africa whenever he could) witnessed the Bingo BSI masterclass, and I found I was able to dictate what I was writing at a perfectly natural speaking pace while still managing easily to keep up using BSI. In fact, this chap, who I will later explain was the kind of Apple employee who is honest rather than only interested in sales, said I typed comfortably quicker than he had seen sighted people do on the software keyboard. But it wasn't just about speed. The Duo, particularly in its folded state, is just the right shape for BSI. I find the Pro Max begins to tire my hands after a while as I have to hold it in position to input Braille. Not so with the Duo. I can't quite describe it, but everything seemed absolutely right in terms of shape, spacing, weight and balance. It was a pleasure. I can't put it more tangibly than that. A word on calibration: it appears that dot positions are calibrated on the Duo, folded or unfolded, in the same way as they are on most iPhones. That is to say, dots 4-5-6 followed by dots 1-2-3. If you have Voiceover hints enabled, Voiceover will tell you this is how to do it. I tried the 18 Pro way just to see if it worked. It doesn't. It's definitely the traditional way. The Tent, the Laptop and the Enormous Hand A quick word on other modes available. Unfolded Portrait is what Dave describes as like having a giant iPhone. Sorry, Dave, But that doesn't go far enough. Perhaps, and it is a big perhaps, Hagrid would find unfolded Portrait useful, but I cannot think who else would. I certainly did not and will say no more about it. The other two modes are Tent Mode and Laptop Mode. In Tent Mode, the Duo is in the classic tent shape i.e. halfway between folded and unfolded. The tent roof is composed half of the titanium back of the phone (which incidentally feels exquisite to hold), and half of the outer display. Laptop mode is simply the tent turned upside down. Half the inner display rests on the table. The other half is the lid of your laptop. What are they for? I'll leave it to our South African friend now that he knows South Africa are 45-0 up at half time, to do the honours of explaining: Tent Mode is if you want to watch movies. Laptop Mode is when you want to pretend you're a novelist. I'm with Dave on this one. No use for either. But I have no sight at all, and I'd be interested to hear from someone who tries Tent Mode to watch telly in particular. Trade-Offs and Compromises As Forgive me, folks, but as our South African friend is about to feature more in our story, I do wish I'd asked the poor fellow his name. Why didn't I? Alas I have no answer to that question. Anyway we started talking about trade-offs such as no Action Button. He confirmed that he had no idea why this was and that there was no official line on it, but thought it might be possible to use the Camera Control as a quasi-Action Button by reassigning it in settings. I know this can be done on the 16 Pro Max, but I can't recall to what extent and I did not try with the Duo today. Certainly, I don't think the Camera Control can be assigned to perform functions like switching to silent mode, which you can set the Action Button to do. by the way, the Camera Control looks very similar to the Side Button on the Duo, to the extent that I tried summoning Siri with the Camera Control by mistake on one occasion. In addition, there does not appear to be any old-style mute switch on the Duo, which I thought there might be given the absence of the Action Button. Our South African friend and I also discussed the absence of the LiDAR sensor. Now, I don't use Door Detection, People Detection or Point and Speak. I've just never found I wanted to, but if you do, you won't be able to use them in the same way. As our friend explained, LiDAR gives you distances, so the Duo won't be able to do that. However, we then tried VoiceOver's Scene Recognition with both the Duo and the iPhone 18 Pro to see what extra information the phone with the LiDAR sensor would give us, both phones obviously running Visual Intelligence. My honest opinion? There was so little difference between the two descriptions as to be of no account. Even our friend was quite surprised, though he went on very honestly to say that in his view, features like Door Detection are not as good as they have been in the past. For me, these features don't matter. If they matter to you, the Duo's not your bag. Our friend was also very forthcoming on durability and battery. The battery, said he, is up with the Pro in his experience if you use it folded most of the time. unfolded, you will obviously get less. To the extent that some people say you get a lot less, well all I can say (and our friend agreed with me) is that the novelty of being able to fold and unfold our diplomatic passport of a Duo means one's likely to do it rather a lot to begin with. It's a new toy, after all. Speaking of which, I've already mentioned that the hardware seems very, very robust. This was one of the issues on which I was most sceptical and my fears have been entirely assuaged. There is always AppleCare, but even without that readers should remember that in many countries including the UK, the US, Australia and all member states of the European Union, you also have your statutory consumer rights as to fitness for purpose on which to rely. Moreover, our friend told me that AppleCare for a Duo includes replacement of the layer that might get a little worn out or creased if it becomes unpleasant under the fingers in due course. Finally, our friend confirmed what I've always suspected: whereas he himself is a Face ID fan, he's finding that more people than he bargained for like Touch ID. That's great to know for fans of the fingerprint like myself. Why can't we have both, eh? Live and let live, I say. Our friend also confirmed that the Duo is selling very well, just behind the Pro Max, at Brent Cross—an interesting observation from what is a flagship London store. So it seems sighted people are prepared to make the camera trade-offs too. I found that surprising, but gratifying now I am a Duo man. Conclusions—Why I am Sold I love iPhones, and I lov iPads. This is both. It's presented in a genuine pocket-sized form factor, is a joy with BSI, feels and sounds great, and has Touch ID, which is not only convenient but also serves as an open invitation for those who get up specially early every morning to moan about blind Touch ID obsessives to launch a fresh crusade in the comments thread! As I explored the Duo, I imagined being able to unlock my phone on the Tube without dragging the iPhone out of my trouser pocket (it wen't fit the jacket) and waving it in front of my face. I imagined watching TV with those wonderful speakers in unfolded landscape and lovely speakers, it no longer mattering if I'd forgotten the portable Bluetooth one. I imagined easier games of chess and backgammon on a tablet-like screen. I imagined breaking off reading the newspaper in Easy Reader on the right hand side to send a quick WhatsApp message on the left, before returning to the paper, with the added bonus of knowing exactly where the splitter is. I have written this whole post on my 16 Pro Max, and by comparison it's somewhat cumbersome. Sure, there are trade-offs, and I have a great deal of sympathy with the argument that if you're paying as much as you are for the Duo, you should surely not have to compromise on anything. Additionally, some compromises such as the absence of an Action Button are difficult to fathom. Nevertheless, I'll live with the trade-offs. They are far outweighed by the attractions. I hope you've found this review, for want of a better word, helpful. I'm looking forward to reading other people's observations, and I don't just mean those of the Face ID merchants. Author's note: The pizzeria mentioned in the introduction to this article has pepperoni, bacon and mushroom, and cheeseburger pizzas as meat options. They are not deep pan but are decent Italian bases. The author can attest that they are an ideal snack en route out of the shopping centre. One slice will keep you going just fine.

For me, and accidental though this benefit may be, I preferred it to the iPad because of this.

I was in a very busy Apple Store, so bear that in mind. Additionally, the only settings I changed were to enable BSI's quick activation gesture. I played no music and listened to no books. Nevertheless, I thought Daniel compact sounded very good, both in folded and unfolded landscape modes. Indeed, the latter reminded me of the beautiful audio that I used to get from the iPad Pro. I would therefore conclude that Apple must be doing something right with this. Was it any better than the audio from the iPhone 18 Pro, which I also tried? In unfolded landscape, I would say it was, though if you're in the market for a Pro and you have a 16 Pro Max like I do, I would immediately agree that the 18 Pro is a big step up from that, and worth it for the audio alone.

I had really wanted to try this and I was blown away. In unfolded Landscape, the Duo was a breeze for BSI in tabletop mode. I tried typing as fast as the cable on the table would allow in a blank note in the notes app and made hardly any errors. Those I did make were down to the unfortunate stoop I had to adopt owing to the cable on the table aforesaid, compounded by Voiceover's being set to speak both characters and words—I had forgotten how utterly tiresome I find that much keyboard echo and how it appears to slow one down. I then folded the phone and tried it in Screen Away Mode. All I can say is the speed of my Landscape tabletop typing was blasted out of the water. Again, I tried to braille as fast as I could and I can't remember making any errors. Indeed, an Apple Store employee (a South African gentleman who rather unconvincingly assured me he wasn't sneakily checking the rugby score between Italy and South Africa whenever he could) witnessed the Bingo BSI masterclass, and I found I was able to dictate what I was writing at a perfectly natural speaking pace while still managing easily to keep up using BSI. In fact, this chap, who I will later explain was the kind of Apple employee who is honest rather than only interested in sales, said I typed comfortably quicker than he had seen sighted people do on the software keyboard.

But it wasn't just about speed. The Duo, particularly in its folded state, is just the right shape for BSI. I find the Pro Max begins to tire my hands after a while as I have to hold it in position to input Braille. Not so with the Duo. I can't quite describe it, but everything seemed absolutely right in terms of shape, spacing, weight and balance. It was a pleasure. I can't put it more tangibly than that.

A word on calibration: it appears that dot positions are calibrated on the Duo, folded or unfolded, in the same way as they are on most iPhones. That is to say, dots 4-5-6 followed by dots 1-2-3. If you have Voiceover hints enabled, Voiceover will tell you this is how to do it. I tried the 18 Pro way just to see if it worked. It doesn't. It's definitely the traditional way.

A quick word on other modes available. Unfolded Portrait is what Dave describes as like having a giant iPhone. Sorry, Dave, But that doesn't go far enough. Perhaps, and it is a big perhaps, Hagrid would find unfolded Portrait useful, but I cannot think who else would. I certainly did not and will say no more about it.

The other two modes are Tent Mode and Laptop Mode. In Tent Mode, the Duo is in the classic tent shape i.e. halfway between folded and unfolded. The tent roof is composed half of the titanium back of the phone (which incidentally feels exquisite to hold), and half of the outer display. Laptop mode is simply the tent turned upside down. Half the inner display rests on the table. The other half is the lid of your laptop. What are they for? I'll leave it to our South African friend now that he knows South Africa are 45-0 up at half time, to do the honours of explaining: Tent Mode is if you want to watch movies. Laptop Mode is when you want to pretend you're a novelist.

I'm with Dave on this one. No use for either. But I have no sight at all, and I'd be interested to hear from someone who tries Tent Mode to watch telly in particular.

As Forgive me, folks, but as our South African friend is about to feature more in our story, I do wish I'd asked the poor fellow his name. Why didn't I? Alas I have no answer to that question. Anyway we started talking about trade-offs such as no Action Button. He confirmed that he had no idea why this was and that there was no official line on it, but thought it might be possible to use the Camera Control as a quasi-Action Button by reassigning it in settings. I know this can be done on the 16 Pro Max, but I can't recall to what extent and I did not try with the Duo today. Certainly, I don't think the Camera Control can be assigned to perform functions like switching to silent mode, which you can set the Action Button to do. by the way, the Camera Control looks very similar to the Side Button on the Duo, to the extent that I tried summoning Siri with the Camera Control by mistake on one occasion. In addition, there does not appear to be any old-style mute switch on the Duo, which I thought there might be given the absence of the Action Button.

Our South African friend and I also discussed the absence of the LiDAR sensor. Now, I don't use Door Detection, People Detection or Point and Speak. I've just never found I wanted to, but if you do, you won't be able to use them in the same way. As our friend explained, LiDAR gives you distances, so the Duo won't be able to do that. However, we then tried VoiceOver's Scene Recognition with both the Duo and the iPhone 18 Pro to see what extra information the phone with the LiDAR sensor would give us, both phones obviously running Visual Intelligence. My honest opinion? There was so little difference between the two descriptions as to be of no account. Even our friend was quite surprised, though he went on very honestly to say that in his view, features like Door Detection are not as good as they have been in the past. For me, these features don't matter. If they matter to you, the Duo's not your bag.

Our friend was also very forthcoming on durability and battery. The battery, said he, is up with the Pro in his experience if you use it folded most of the time. unfolded, you will obviously get less. To the extent that some people say you get a lot less, well all I can say (and our friend agreed with me) is that the novelty of being able to fold and unfold our diplomatic passport of a Duo means one's likely to do it rather a lot to begin with. It's a new toy, after all. Speaking of which, I've already mentioned that the hardware seems very, very robust. This was one of the issues on which I was most sceptical and my fears have been entirely assuaged. There is always AppleCare, but even without that readers should remember that in many countries including the UK, the US, Australia and all member states of the European Union, you also have your statutory consumer rights as to fitness for purpose on which to rely. Moreover, our friend told me that AppleCare for a Duo includes replacement of the layer that might get a little worn out or creased if it becomes unpleasant under the fingers in due course.

Finally, our friend confirmed what I've always suspected: whereas he himself is a Face ID fan, he's finding that more people than he bargained for like Touch ID. That's great to know for fans of the fingerprint like myself. Why can't we have both, eh? Live and let live, I say. Our friend also confirmed that the Duo is selling very well, just behind the Pro Max, at Brent Cross—an interesting observation from what is a flagship London store. So it seems sighted people are prepared to make the camera trade-offs too. I found that surprising, but gratifying now I am a Duo man.

I love iPhones, and I lov iPads. This is both. It's presented in a genuine pocket-sized form factor, is a joy with BSI, feels and sounds great, and has Touch ID, which is not only convenient but also serves as an open invitation for those who get up specially early every morning to moan about blind Touch ID obsessives to launch a fresh crusade in the comments thread! As I explored the Duo, I imagined being able to unlock my phone on the Tube without dragging the iPhone out of my trouser pocket (it wen't fit the jacket) and waving it in front of my face. I imagined watching TV with those wonderful speakers in unfolded landscape and lovely speakers, it no longer mattering if I'd forgotten the portable Bluetooth one. I imagined easier games of chess and backgammon on a tablet-like screen. I imagined breaking off reading the newspaper in Easy Reader on the right hand side to send a quick WhatsApp message on the left, before returning to the paper, with the added bonus of knowing exactly where the splitter is. I have written this whole post on my 16 Pro Max, and by comparison it's somewhat cumbersome. Sure, there are trade-offs, and I have a great deal of sympathy with the argument that if you're paying as much as you are for the Duo, you should surely not have to compromise on anything. Additionally, some compromises such as the absence of an Action Button are difficult to fathom. Nevertheless, I'll live with the trade-offs. They are far outweighed by the attractions.

I hope you've found this review, for want of a better word, helpful. I'm looking forward to reading other people's observations, and I don't just mean those of the Face ID merchants.

Author's note:

The pizzeria mentioned in the introduction to this article has pepperoni, bacon and mushroom, and cheeseburger pizzas as meat options. They are not deep pan but are decent Italian bases. The author can attest that they are an ideal snack en route out of the shopping centre. One slice will keep you going just fine.

en.title: Everlife 2 - Life Simulator
en.summary: Build a life. Then build a legacy. Everlife 2 is a free life simulator with no ads and over a million words of story. Grow up, fall in love, chase a career, make a few terrible decisions, and leave a family behind to deal with them. • More than 13,000 cards across school, love, work, family, health, crime and fame • Branching storylines that unfold over years, with multiple endings • 350 jobs, dozens of skills and over 120 kinds of creative projects • 14 towns, each with its own scenery, climate, holiday, stories and elections • Play for generations as your heirs inherit the money, the house and the consequences ONE SEASON AT A TIME Spend each season's energy on your life, your people and your world, then tap Next Season and see what comes back. The Chaos slider runs from quiet suburb to total meltdown, and Classic mode keeps it to one action a season. CREATE SOMEONE. SEE WHO THEY BECOME. Choose their looks, hometown, family, backstory, traits and conditions. Traits come in opposite pairs, like Workaholic and Slacker, and your choices can earn new ones. Your backstory comes back later in life with stories of its own. STORIES THAT REMEMBER One card today can follow you for years. Storylines remember what you chose and how you treated the people in them, then end good, bittersweet, chaotic or secret. GROW UP YOUR WAY Survive grades, cliques, clubs and crushes with the kids from your street. Then apply to college, join Greek life, or skip it and start working. MAKE A LIVING Build a resume, survive the interview and climb ten ranks with pay that matches the real-world job. Answer to a boss, outshine a rival and sweat your yearly review. Or turn to crime. It pays well, until it doesn't. TURN TALENT INTO SOMETHING REAL Master skills to unlock perks, then risk money and time on projects that can fail. Write a novel, record an album, shoot a feature film, design a clothing line or build a personal robot. A hit can pay royalties for years. MONEY IS REAL Track real dollars, net worth and social class. Take out loans, invest, or bid at the auction house. Fall behind and the collectors call. Divorce splits what you own. LOVE, FIGHT, FORGIVE, REPEAT Date, move in, propose, marry, cheat, divorce, reconcile, or let an ex return with excellent timing and terrible intentions. Meet the in-laws, fight for custody, and care for your parents as they age. RAISE A FAMILY Plan a pregnancy, try IVF, hire a surrogate, adopt, or decide parenthood isn't for this life. Watch years of parenting shape the adult your child becomes. Adopt a pet from the shelter too: 21 species and over 100 breeds. MAKE A HOME IN A WORLD THAT MOVES Buy a hometown house or a vacation home in another town, add a recording studio or a pool, and live with a home that's cozy, moldy or haunted. Celebrate eight holidays a year, ride out snow days and heatwaves, and vote for mayor or run yourself. FACE THE HARD YEARS Health problems start as symptoms before they get a name. See a doctor, weigh therapy, medication and insurance, and live with what follows. Injuries, cravings, grief and dementia can reshape a life. So can recovery. EVERY LIFE LEAVES SOMETHING BEHIND When your character dies, read the obituary, hold the funeral and settle the will. Then start over, resurrect, or play on as your heir with the money, heirlooms and unfinished business you left behind. Chase dynasty goals, unlock nearly 200 achievements, and spend Fate to give the next generation a head start. PLAY ON YOUR TERMS Everlife 2 is free and fully offline in 13 languages, with no ads, no wait timers and no premium currency. One life is only the beginning. How will you live your Everlife?

en.title: Nano Empire 2
en.summary: Once, nanobots gave humans godlike power to create worlds, limited only by their imagination. But now the Creators have lost control of the creations! You, a humble starship captain, are all that stands between the galaxy and destruction. Nano Empire 2 is an incremental sandbox text adventure, featuring 30 handcrafted worlds where dreams have turned into nightmares. Endless beach parties suddenly have a leviathan problem. Crystal automata rise up against the Queen of Light. A rogue nanobot factory produces strangely beautiful horrors. A royal family of sentient trees has forgotten how to reproduce. There are also vampires, inverted merpeople, and a Great Clown Head. And of course, all these factions are at war... Without nanobots meeting everyone's needs automatically, ship captains like you are about to become the most important people in the galaxy. Transport resources to populations who desperately need them, take sides in wars or profit from both sides, befriend eccentric creatures, grow your fleet, and maybe even research a way to undo the damage. Every world has a dramatically different vision for the future of civilization, and your choices will determine which one is successful. You don't need to have played Nano Empire 1 to enjoy this game, but returning players will notice many recurring characters... -Will Peter Frederick ever grow up and care about something other than partying? -Will Zithguul the giant scorpion escape from the Petting Zoo? -What will happen with Roland, Carla, and the ongoing conflict between the Underworld and the Core?* Features: -100% human-written. No generative AI was used to make this game. -Simple and elegant resource management as in Nano Empire 1. All the storytelling of an open world space opera with none of the tedious inventory management. -30 factions playing out a dynamic simulation of economy, war, and culture. Every action you take affects the balance of power. -Several days of idle gameplay. Each world unlocks new activities over time as it grows. -Collect artifacts and allies with world-shattering effects (sometimes literally). -Over 40 possible endings! (You can experience multiple endings without having to restart the game every time. A handy Ending Tracker is included.) -Play the complete game for free with no ads. An in-app purchase is available to unlock optional worlds and bonus resources. -Fully accessible with VoiceOver. *If you haven't already figured it out, this game takes place after the most interesting ending of Nano Empire: the one with the apocalypse...

en.title: FruitPot Adventures
en.summary: A luxury hotel, a missing necklace, and a resourceful detective. Enjoy hours of fun in a free mystery adventure you can play offline, with VoiceOver support. Join James F. Pot as he investigates the Golden Lion Hotel. Talk to its quirky guests, uncover clues, try on disguises, and combine items to solve situations that are as puzzling as they are hilarious. HOURS OF FUN AND CLEVER PUZZLES Explore the hotel and tackle logic, memory, and sound puzzles. Every conversation and every item could help you move forward. Sometimes you’ll need a tool. Sometimes, a disguise. And almost always, a little ingenuity. PLAY OFFLINE, AT YOUR OWN PACE Play without an internet connection and take your investigation wherever you go. Automatic saving keeps your progress safe, and three save slots let you organize your adventures. ACCESSIBILITY THAT LETS YOU EXPLORE YOUR WAY • VoiceOver support. • Descriptions of scenes, objects, and characters. • Guided controls to browse, select, and describe elements around you. • Customizable voice narration. • Separate volume controls for music, ambient sounds, voices, and sound effects. • Options for larger buttons and more vivid colors. • Map zoom to explore the details. • Reduced animation and outlines for interactive areas. FOR IPHONE AND IPAD Enjoy retro-style scenery, music, and memorable characters, with text in English, Spanish, French, German and Italian. THE COMPLETE GAME IS FREE No ads and no payments required to continue the story. You can finish the entire adventure for free. If you’d like to support future adventures, you’ll find four optional contribution levels under the star on the main menu. Each level unlocks a supporter emblem, without gameplay advantages or content needed to finish the adventure. Contributions require an internet connection to the App Store. There’s a mystery waiting at the Golden Lion. James F. Pot has just arrived.
