es.title: Nuevo curso de introducción a Python de NVDA.es y otras actualizaciones
es.summary: ¡Hola, comunidad! Llevábamos tiempo sin traer novedades por aquí. Aprovechando que NVDA 2026.3.1 está al caer, hemos pensado que era un buen momento. En esta entrada te hablamos de la A11yconf 2026, nuestra nueva plataforma de formación y el nuevo curso que estrenamos junto a ella, y el cifrado de datos en TeleNVDA. ¡Comenzamos! A11yconf … Continuar leyendo "Nuevo curso de introducción a Python de NVDA.es y otras actualizaciones" La entrada Nuevo curso de introducción a Python de NVDA.es y otras actualizaciones se publicó primero en NVDA en español .
es.body:
¡Hola, comunidad! Llevábamos tiempo sin traer novedades por aquí. Aprovechando que NVDA 2026.3.1 está al caer, hemos pensado que era un buen momento. En esta entrada te hablamos de la A11yconf 2026, nuestra nueva plataforma de formación y el nuevo curso que estrenamos junto a ella, y el cifrado de datos en TeleNVDA. ¡Comenzamos!

La A11yconf del año pasado salió muy bien, hasta el punto de que este año han repetido. Nosotros, por nuestra parte, también hemos repetido patrocinando el evento y echando una mano para que dispongan de los recursos necesarios. Este año, la A11yconf tendrá lugar el 28 de noviembre en Zaragoza. Si todavía no tienes tu entrada, ¡te aconsejamos comprarla cuanto antes! Visita la página de la A11yconf En esta ocasión no disponemos de stand independiente, pero estaremos en el recinto. ¡No dudes en preguntar por nosotros si vas por allí!

La inteligencia artificial generativa ha venido a revolucionar nuestra forma de trabajar, sin importar el sector. Si tenemos un ordenador delante, ya es habitual hablar de Claude, Gemini o GPT. Y en el desarrollo de NVDA no podía ser menos: es raro el día que no aparece un complemento nuevo en la tienda internacional. Montones de nuevos autores construyen y comparten complementos cuyo desarrollo ha sido asistido o enteramente realizado por la IA. A priori, esto suena a cambio positivo. Sin embargo, la realidad es muy distinta. A menudo nos encontramos complementos que duplican funciones existentes de otros complementos, están plagados de fallos, o añaden funciones que ya vienen en el propio NVDA. La tienda está llena de traductores, descargadores de Youtube, reproductores de radio, y complementos para preguntar a la IA, entre otros. Muchas personas que no se conocen entre sí tienen la misma idea. La IA, que tiende cada vez más a dar el mismo resultado con las mismas condiciones de partida, elabora complementos con sutiles diferencias, que en esencia son iguales y pueden coincidir hasta en nombre. A la falta de análisis previo se unen la falta de conocimientos en programación y la ausencia de juicio crítico. Muchos de los autores que han sumado complementos a la tienda no tienen conocimientos de programación, y por tanto son incapaces de defender por sí mismos sus propias creaciones. Con este panorama, estamos seguros de que entenderás por qué sólo se actualizan complementos clásicos en el catálogo de nuestra comunidad, y por qué no añadimos complementos nuevos. Los esfuerzos necesarios para filtrar y revisar se han disparado hasta un punto que, con el escaso tiempo que tenemos, se ha vuelto inasumible. Así que hemos decidido entrar en acción utilizando exactamente la misma herramienta que causa el problema: la IA. Bien usada, la inteligencia artificial constituye una herramienta muy potente. Gracias a ella, hemos preparado un curso en el que, paradójicamente, el uso de IA está prohibido, así como el uso de entornos de desarrollo con autocompletado e indentado automático. Se trata de un curso de introducción a Python que ayuda a sentar las bases del lenguaje y enseña a obtener información de Internet y crear interfaces gráficas. Quien supere el curso será capaz de leer código fuente, ya sea de NVDA o de un complemento, y comprender lo que hará el intérprete con ese código. Como bien han podido comprobar los participantes de nuestra prueba piloto, el curso entraña cierta dificultad, y no es el típico que se saca en dos tardes: además de los conceptos teóricos, existen ejercicios prácticos, todos de respuesta abierta y corregidos a mano. Queremos que aprendas a programar en condiciones, interiorizando cada concepto. Las herramientas que uses después, ya son cosa tuya, pero tendrás la capacidad de juzgar el resultado. El acceso al curso es totalmente gratuito. Opcionalmente, al acabar, podrás comprar un certificado de aprovechamiento, en el que también contemplamos descuentos para personas que pasen por dificultades económicas. El curso funciona sobre una plataforma de formación propia, también construida con la ayuda de la IA. Puedes ver su código fuente en este repositorio y conectarte directamente a ella en la siguiente dirección: https://formacion.nvda.es . ¡Te esperamos!

En los protocolos y programas de control remoto con NVDA, la seguridad siempre ha tenido una prioridad crítica. NVDA es un lector de pantalla que capta, procesa y devuelve un montón de información que puede contener datos sensibles y jugarnos una mala pasada si cae en malas manos. Tradicionalmente, las conexiones entre el complemento y los servidores de control se cifraban con un certificado SSL, pero esto no impide que un propietario malintencionado de un servidor pueda interceptar y descifrar las comunicaciones. Por eso, TeleNVDA añade una capa de seguridad extra: el cifrado de datos. No lo hemos querido llamar cifrado de extremo a extremo, porque no lo es, pero impedirá que el propietario del servidor descifre lo que está pasando, así que en ese sentido se le parece. Cuando te conectes, comprobarás que, además del típico campo de clave, existe otro que permite introducir una contraseña adicional. Si lo rellenas, los datos se cifran con AES-GCM-256, de tal forma que sólo los miembros de la sesión que conozcan las dos contraseñas podrán unirse y participar con normalidad en el control remoto. Por desgracia, esta segunda contraseña acaba con la compatibilidad con el soporte remoto integrado en NVDA. Si necesitas garantizar compatibilidad, basta con no rellenarla. ¿Todavía no ves este campo? Es posible que tu TeleNVDA esté sin actualizar. Descarga aquí la versión más reciente Esto es todo por ahora. En breve volveremos para hablar de NVDA 2026.3.1 y sus correcciones de seguridad. ¡Hasta la próxima!

La entrada Nuevo curso de introducción a Python de NVDA.es y otras actualizaciones se publicó primero en NVDA en español .

es.title: Eva: la inteligencia artificial que adapta unas gafas inteligentes a las necesidades visuales de cada persona
es.summary: La inteligencia artificial continúa abriendo nuevas posibilidades para mejorar la autonomía de las personas con discapacidad visual. La última propuesta llega de la mano de Eyedaptic, una empresa especializada en tecnología de mejora visual que acaba de anunciar el lanzamiento de Eva, un asistente inteligente integrado en sus gafas EYE7. La principal novedad es que […] La entrada Eva: la inteligencia artificial que adapta unas gafas inteligentes a las necesidades visuales de cada persona se publicó primero en Conticgo .
es.body:
La inteligencia artificial continúa abriendo nuevas posibilidades para mejorar la autonomía de las personas con discapacidad visual. La última propuesta llega de la mano de Eyedaptic , una empresa especializada en tecnología de mejora visual que acaba de anunciar el lanzamiento de Eva, un asistente inteligente integrado en sus gafas EYE7.

La principal novedad es que Eva no se limita a describir lo que aparece delante de la cámara. También puede interpretar lo que necesita el usuario y actuar sobre las funciones de mejora visual de las gafas.

Hasta ahora, muchas herramientas de asistencia visual basadas en inteligencia artificial se han centrado en reconocer objetos, leer textos o describir escenas. Eva pretende ir un paso más allá.

Su funcionamiento se basa en la interpretación de instrucciones expresadas mediante lenguaje natural. Esto permite que la persona pueda comunicarse con las gafas de una manera más intuitiva, sin necesidad de aprender comandos específicos.

Por ejemplo, si alguien está intentando leer un cartel y dice «no consigo leer eso», Eva puede interpretar la petición y ajustar la experiencia visual para facilitar la lectura.

De esta manera, la tecnología no solo proporciona información sobre el entorno, sino que también puede modificar determinados ajustes de las gafas para adaptarlos a la actividad que se está realizando.

Según Eyedaptic, el asistente está diseñado para ayudar en diferentes situaciones de la vida cotidiana. Entre sus aplicaciones se encuentran:

Además, la compañía indica que Eva permite comunicarse en hasta 99 idiomas, lo que amplía sus posibilidades de utilización.

Eva está integrada en las gafas EYE7 de Eyedaptic, un dispositivo que combina tecnología de visión artificial, inteligencia artificial y realidad aumentada.

Estas gafas incorporan pantallas de alta definición y diferentes funciones de mejora visual. Su objetivo es ayudar a las personas con pérdida de visión central, especialmente aquellas con enfermedades de la retina como la degeneración macular asociada a la edad (DMAE).

Una de sus características es que las funciones pueden controlarse mediante instrucciones de voz, lo que permite interactuar con el dispositivo sin tener que manejar constantemente sus controles.

La llegada de Eva refuerza esta propuesta: la inteligencia artificial puede interpretar las necesidades de la persona y actuar directamente sobre las funciones de mejora visual disponibles.

Eyedaptic ha comunicado que, durante sus pruebas internas, Eva alcanzó una precisión superior al 99 % en lectura y del 97 % en la interpretación de comandos.

La empresa también señala que el asistente ya está disponible para los usuarios de EYE7 mediante una actualización remota del software, por lo que no es necesario adquirir unas gafas nuevas para incorporar esta función.

No obstante, estas cifras deben interpretarse con cautela. Se trata de resultados comunicados por el fabricante y no de una evaluación independiente publicada en una revista científica. Será necesario conocer su funcionamiento en situaciones reales y con diferentes perfiles de discapacidad visual para valorar su utilidad.

La propuesta de Eyedaptic refleja una tendencia cada vez más presente en la tiflotecnología: desarrollar herramientas que no solo proporcionen información sobre el entorno, sino que también se adapten a las necesidades de cada persona.

Para quienes tienen baja visión, poder ajustar una ayuda visual mediante una conversación sencilla puede facilitar determinadas actividades y reducir la necesidad de navegar por menús o aprender controles específicos.

Sin embargo, estas soluciones deben entenderse como herramientas de apoyo. No recuperan la visión ni sustituyen la rehabilitación visual, las ayudas ópticas o los dispositivos de movilidad.

El verdadero potencial de Eva dependerá de su rendimiento en el día a día, de su facilidad de uso y de cómo responda a las necesidades reales de las personas con discapacidad visual.

Si te ha gustado esta noticia no te pierdas las últimas novedades en tiflotectnología en nuestro apartado de noticias y redes sociales .

Fuente de la noticia: Eyedaptic .

en.title: Getting the Most Out of Vispero Companion: Tips and Best Practices
en.summary: Vispero Companion has grown from a helpful question-and-answer assistant into your one conversational home for all the AI features in JAWS. Whether you want to know how a feature works, get a description of a photo, explore a busy web page, or have a task done for you, it all happens in one familiar, accessible …
en.body:
Vispero Companion has grown from a helpful question-and-answer assistant into your one conversational home for all the AI features in JAWS. Whether you want to know how a feature works, get a description of a photo, explore a busy web page, or have a task done for you, it all happens in one familiar, accessible window. And because everything lives in a single conversation, you can keep asking follow-up questions without starting over. Here are some tips and best practices for getting the most out of Vispero Companion.

With Vispero Companion Actions, Companion does more than answer questions. Just ask, and it can help you:

You’re always in control. Companion only works when you ask, asks for your approval before executing important steps, and stops immediately when you press ESC.

The new Vispero Companion is available through the Early Adopter Program to users in the United States who are signed in to a Vispero account. To turn it on:

Once it’s on, press JAWS KEY+SPACEBAR followed by F1 to open Companion. The JAWS key is INSERT when using Desktop Keyboard layout, and CAPS LOCK when using Laptop layout.

Companion looks at what is on your screen to understand what you’re asking about. If the application window isn’t maximized, content can be cut off at the edges, and Companion may even pick up parts of other windows, such as the taskbar. Before you ask for help, place focus in the application you are working in and press WINDOWS+UP ARROW to maximize it.

When Companion carries out a task for you, it moves to your application and works there, much as you would. If you type, click, switch windows, or open another program while it’s working, you can change what Companion sees and pull it away from the task. It’s best to leave the keyboard and mouse alone until the task is complete, and Companion will let you know what it did once it’s finished. If you need to stop it, press ESC .

Once Companion takes its first action in an application, it stays in that app for the rest of the conversation. Outlook and Word, for example, are treated as separate applications. If you want help with something in a different program such as a web browser, close Companion and relaunch it from that application.

Companion opens in its own window, just like any other application on your computer. When you’re finished with it, press ALT+F4 to close it, the same way you would close any other window.

You don’t need to know which feature or setting does the job. Just tell Companion what you need, for example:

The more detail you give, the fewer attempts Companion needs to get it right. “For example, if you are asking Companion to help you book a flight, “Set the departure date to November 14” will work better than “Select November 14,” because Companion will know which type of date you want to set.

Companion keeps track of your current conversation while it is open so you can ask a follow-up question or for the next step without starting over. When you’re ready to change topics, select New Request for a fresh start or close and then relaunch Companion from a different application.

Already have the Picture Smart and Page Explorer commands in muscle memory? Keep using them. They now bring their results right into Companion, where you can ask follow-up questions.

Companion asks before doing anything that can’t easily be undone, such as submitting a form. Take a moment to read what it’s about to do before you confirm, and check its report when the task is finished so you know exactly where things stand.

Your feedback shapes what comes next for Companion. Select Give Feedback beside New Request to rate an answer or leave a comment. This button requires the Submit Anonymous Usage Data (telemetry) option to be turned on. If you’d prefer to leave it off, email your comments to SoftwareSuggestions@vispero.com . You can also select the Send Feedback button in the JAWS Early Adopter Program dialog.

For more information and a live demo, join us for our webinar on new features of JAWS, ZoomText, and Fusion 2027 at noon ET on Thursday, November 12. Have questions? Send an email to training@vispero.com .

Cookie Voice Recipes is a voice-first recipe app built for blind and low-vision cooks. You can find recipes, have them read aloud, and move through ingredients and steps hands-free by voice, so you can cook without needing to touch or look at your phone.

Voice commands can be used to repeat steps or ask about ingredient quantities. The app was developed with input from blind and low-vision users, including user testing with vision rehabilitation teachers.

Free or paid:

All buttons and controls have accessible labels, and the core cooking flow—including reading ingredients, moving to the next or previous step, and repeating a step—can be used entirely by voice without touching the screen.

es.title: GRETA & STARKS y ConUnPack impulsan la accesibilidad en las salas de cine españolas
es.summary: Las personas con discapacidad visual o auditiva podrán acceder a recursos de accesibilidad durante las sesiones habituales de cine gracias a soluciones como GRETA. La compañía tecnológica GRETA & STARKS y la distribuidora española ConUnPack han anunciado una alianza para impulsar el uso de esta tecnología en las salas españolas. La iniciativa se presenta en […] La entrada GRETA & STARKS y ConUnPack impulsan la accesibilidad en las salas de cine españolas se publicó primero en Conticgo .
es.body:
Las personas con discapacidad visual o auditiva podrán acceder a recursos de accesibilidad durante las sesiones habituales de cine gracias a soluciones como GRETA. La compañía tecnológica GRETA & STARKS y la distribuidora española ConUnPack han anunciado una alianza para impulsar el uso de esta tecnología en las salas españolas.

La iniciativa se presenta en MERCI 2026, el Mercado de Cine Independiente organizado por la Semana Internacional de Cine de Valladolid (SEMINCI) y la Asociación de Distribuidores Independientes Cinematográficos (ADICINE). El encuentro celebra su sexta edición del 28 al 30 de octubre en Valladolid.

GRETA es una aplicación móvil que permite utilizar diferentes recursos de accesibilidad sincronizados con la película. De este modo, cada espectador puede disfrutar de la sesión con los apoyos que necesita desde su propio dispositivo.

Entre sus principales funciones se encuentran:

Según explica la web oficial de GRETA , la aplicación utiliza el reconocimiento del sonido para sincronizar los recursos de accesibilidad con la película. Para utilizarla, basta con un teléfono móvil y, en el caso de la audiodescripción, unos auriculares.

Una de las principales ventajas de esta tecnología es que permite compartir una misma sesión cinematográfica sin necesidad de organizar proyecciones específicas para las personas con discapacidad visual o auditiva.

Cada espectador utiliza de forma individual el recurso que necesita. Así, una persona puede escuchar la audiodescripción mientras el resto del público sigue la película con el sonido habitual de la sala. Del mismo modo, los subtítulos adaptados pueden consultarse en la pantalla del teléfono móvil.

Esta posibilidad favorece una experiencia cinematográfica compartida y contribuye a reducir las barreras de acceso a la cultura.

No obstante, es importante tener en cuenta que la aplicación no garantiza la accesibilidad de todos los títulos. Para utilizar sus funciones, la película debe contar con los recursos correspondientes y estar disponible en el catálogo.

La alianza entre GRETA & STARKS y ConUnPack busca acercar estas soluciones a los profesionales de la exhibición cinematográfica en España.

Una de las ventajas del sistema es que no requiere instalar equipamiento específico en las salas para que cada usuario pueda utilizar la aplicación. Esto puede facilitar su incorporación en cines independientes y en espacios con menos recursos técnicos.

Sin embargo, la disponibilidad de películas accesibles y las condiciones de implantación del servicio siguen siendo factores importantes. Para ampliar su alcance, resulta fundamental que distribuidoras y exhibidores colaboren para ofrecer más títulos con audiodescripción y subtítulos adaptados.

La alianza se presenta en el marco de MERCI 2026, un encuentro profesional que reúne a representantes de la distribución, la exhibición y otros ámbitos de la industria audiovisual.

La programación oficial de SEMINCI incluye una presentación dedicada al cine accesible con la aplicación GRETA.

Este tipo de iniciativas pone de relieve la importancia de incorporar la accesibilidad a la distribución y exhibición cinematográfica. No basta con que una película llegue a las salas: también es necesario que las personas con diferentes necesidades sensoriales puedan acceder a su contenido.

Desde esta perspectiva, las herramientas de audio descripción y subtitulado adaptado representan un paso más hacia una cultura audiovisual inclusiva.

Si te ha gustado esta noticia no te pierdas las últimas novedades en tiflotectnología en nuestro apartado de noticias y redes sociales .

Fuentes: SEMINCI: programación profesional y MERCI 2026 , GRETA & STARKS: funcionamiento y características de la aplicación , Audiovisual451: información sobre la alianza entre ConUnPack y GRETA & STARKS , Ciné-Sens: información sobre el funcionamiento y la disponibilidad de recursos accesibles .

Se recomienda a todos los usuarios descargar esta versión y proporcionar comentarios por los canales de la comunidad, o por el sistema de informe de fallos de NV Access. es.body:
Tal y como ha anunciado NV Access mediante esta publicación , la rc 1 de NVDA 2026.3.1 ya se encuentra disponible para descarga y pruebas. Se recomienda a todos los usuarios descargar esta versión y proporcionar comentarios por los canales de la comunidad, o por el sistema de informe de fallos de NV Access . A menos que se detecten fallos críticos de última hora, esta versión será idéntica a la versión final de NVDA 2026.3. Esta versión no es apta para entornos de producción. Al instalar esta rc te unirás al canal beta, y sólo recibirás avisos de actualización de compilaciones beta y candidatas a liberación (rc). El canal beta/rc siempre te mantendrá al día con la versión más reciente de NVDA. La última rc de un ciclo de liberación es idéntica a la última versión estable. Para regresar al canal de versiones estables, instala a mano la última versión estable.

Esta versión contiene un parche que resuelve incidencias de seguridad. También corrige un fallo introducido en NVDA 2026.3 con el conmutador de tareas de Windows 10. Se ha restaurado la voz de Espeak NG en portugués de Brasil al comportamiento que tenía en NVDA 2026.2. Para instalar esta rc, puedes configurar el canal «rc y beta» en el complemento Selector del canal de actualización y buscar actualizaciones desde el menú Ayuda de NVDA, o actualizar desde una beta anterior. Y como siempre, también puedes descargar manualmente el instalador de NVDA 2026.3.1 rc 1 . Su suma de comprobación SHA256, que te permitirá garantizar la integridad del archivo descargado, es 25761ace59812a5d60cc7282cca253c78d9293ce3e710eafb2b29783b5a1257c. ¡Feliz miércoles!

Work More Productively with the New Vispero Companion in JAWS Vispero Companion now brings all your AI help together in one place. Whether you want to learn how a feature works, …
en.body:
JAWS, ZoomText, and Fusion 2027 are now available, offering new and exciting features that increase efficiency and productivity. Here’s a look at several highlights.

Vispero Companion now brings all your AI help together in one place. Whether you want to learn how a feature works, get a description of a photo, explore a busy web page, change a setting, or have a task performed for you, just ask Vispero Companion. Because everything lives in a single conversation, you can keep asking follow-up questions without starting over.

Note: The Vispero Companion website is still available for users who need to access product guidance from devices not running JAWS.

A Vispero Account is required to use the new features in the Vispero Companion update.

This feature is part of the Early Adopter Program, which provides access to new functionality that is still under active development. It is intended for users who want to try out upcoming features and provide feedback before they are fully released.

To enable this option:

In response to frequent requests from our community, JAWS now supports MuseScore, a popular free program for writing, editing, and playing back sheet music. Composers, music students, teachers, and hobbyists all use MuseScore to create everything from simple melodies to full orchestral scores, and JAWS users can now join them.

The Smoothing tab in the Preferences dialog box is now the Smoothing and Performance tab, with a new Performance group. The default, Best text quality, uses xFont and geometric smoothing to deliver the sharpest, clearest text ZoomText and Fusion offer, along with support for legacy reading. If ZoomText or Fusion feels slow on your system, you can choose Best performance, which uses geometric smoothing only for faster response, and then return to Best text quality at any time. You can also choose this option in the Startup Wizard.

ZoomText can now magnify apps that use screen-capture protection, so you can still read content that is already shown to you on screen. This is becoming increasingly important, as:

Photo Tracking identifies people, animals, food, and other objects in an image and moves the magnified view directly from one object to the next. You no longer need to zoom and pan across the whole picture to find what you want.

All recognition happens locally on your computer, so Photo Tracking works offline and is suitable for secure environments. It is available in ZoomText Magnifier/Reader, ZoomText Magnifier, and Fusion.

To learn more about all the new features and enhancements in this release, visit the What’s New pages for JAWS , ZoomText , and Fusion 2027.

Note: If you are running the latest version of JAWS, ZoomText, or Fusion and automatic updates are enabled, you can start the download and installation process from the notification.

en.title: AppleVis Unlimited: What's New and Noteworthy for October 2026
en.summary: Welcome to the October 2026 edition of AppleVis Unlimited, your monthly digest of the latest and most notable content on the AppleVis website. This newsletter features a curated selection of community-submitted content, including new app entries, updates, news, podcast episodes, and popular discussions. We hope that you find this publication to be both helpful and informative. If you have any questions or feedback about this newsletter, please feel free to reach out using our Contact Form . AnonyMouse's App Pick of the Month: ReSort: Water Sort Puzzle App If you enjoy relaxing puzzle games that offer just the right amount of challenge, ReSort: Water Sort Puzzle App is definitely worth checking out. This delightful water-sorting game has you moving different colored water between tubes until each contains just one color. It starts out simple, but the puzzles get trickier as you progress, making it surprisingly addictive. With no timers or move limits, you can take your time and enjoy solving each puzzle at your own pace. What really makes ReSort stand out for me is its wonderful sound design. I absolutely love the satisfying pouring sounds, gentle music, and little audio cues that make playing so enjoyable. Add in excellent VoiceOver support, daily challenges, unlockable sounds, and a developer who's been actively listening to the AppleVis community and making improvements based on their feedback, and there's plenty to appreciate. Read more about ReSort here. New Apps ArcFlush: Roguelike Solitaire AI-generated summary of App Store description: A solitaire-inspired roguelike that combines card play with strategic decisions across successive runs. If you enjoy relaxing puzzle games that offer just the right amount of challenge, ReSort: Water Sort Puzzle App is definitely worth checking out. This delightful water-sorting game has you moving different colored water between tubes until each contains just one color. It starts out simple, but the puzzles get trickier as you progress, making it surprisingly addictive. With no timers or move limits, you can take your time and enjoy solving each puzzle at your own pace.

What really makes ReSort stand out for me is its wonderful sound design. I absolutely love the satisfying pouring sounds, gentle music, and little audio cues that make playing so enjoyable. Add in excellent VoiceOver support, daily challenges, unlockable sounds, and a developer who's been actively listening to the AppleVis community and making improvements based on their feedback, and there's plenty to appreciate.

Read more about ReSort here.

es.title: Las gafas inteligentes y la autonomía de las personas con discapacidad visual
es.summary: Las gafas inteligentes y la inteligencia artificial están abriendo nuevas posibilidades para las personas con discapacidad visual. Estas herramientas permiten reconocer establecimientos, leer textos y obtener descripciones del entorno mediante indicaciones de audio. El caso de Daniel Álvarez, que perdió la visión a los 15 años, muestra cómo la tecnología puede facilitar algunas tareas cotidianas. […] La entrada Las gafas inteligentes y la autonomía de las personas con discapacidad visual se publicó primero en Conticgo .
es.body:
Las gafas inteligentes y la inteligencia artificial están abriendo nuevas posibilidades para las personas con discapacidad visual. Estas herramientas permiten reconocer establecimientos, leer textos y obtener descripciones del entorno mediante indicaciones de audio.

El caso de Daniel Álvarez, que perdió la visión a los 15 años, muestra cómo la tecnología puede facilitar algunas tareas cotidianas. Su experiencia, recogida en un reportaje publicado por El Periódico el 25 de octubre de 2026, pone el foco en la utilidad de estos dispositivos para ganar autonomía.

Daniel Álvarez tiene 30 años, estudia Derecho en la Universitat Oberta de Catalunya (UOC) y trabaja en la ONCE. Tras perder la visión por un desprendimiento de retina irreversible, ha incorporado diferentes herramientas tecnológicas a su vida diaria.

Entre ellas destacan las gafas inteligentes, que incorporan cámaras y altavoces. Gracias a las aplicaciones compatibles, puede obtener información sobre los lugares y objetos que tiene delante.

Por ejemplo, estas gafas pueden ayudarle a distinguir si un establecimiento es un supermercado o una peluquería. También permiten leer textos, identificar colores y conocer detalles de objetos o prendas de ropa.

Sin embargo, sus posibilidades todavía tienen limitaciones. La descripción del entorno no siempre es completamente precisa y depende de la información que capta la cámara y de la interpretación que realiza el sistema.

Daniel utiliza, entre otras herramientas, ScribeMe, una aplicación que describe mediante inteligencia artificial las imágenes captadas por las cámaras de las gafas.

Las aplicaciones de inteligencia artificial no se limitan a describir objetos o espacios. También pueden contribuir a mejorar la accesibilidad de documentos y materiales educativos.

En el caso de Daniel, estas herramientas le permiten adaptar información que no está disponible en un formato accesible. Por ejemplo, puede transformar gráficos de ejercicios académicos en descripciones textuales que pueda comprender mediante su lector de pantalla.

Además, utiliza la inteligencia artificial para crear aplicaciones adaptadas a sus propias necesidades.

Estas posibilidades muestran que la tecnología puede facilitar el acceso a la educación, al trabajo y a la información. No obstante, para aprovecharlas es importante que las aplicaciones y los contenidos digitales sean accesibles desde su diseño.

Aunque las gafas inteligentes ofrecen nuevas posibilidades, no sustituyen a las herramientas tradicionales de orientación y movilidad.

Daniel continúa utilizando su bastón y las técnicas de orientación que conoce. Las gafas le aportan información adicional sobre su entorno, pero no garantizan una descripción completa ni una orientación espacial precisa.

Esta distinción es importante. Reconocer un establecimiento o leer un cartel puede resultar útil durante un desplazamiento, pero no equivale a detectar todos los obstáculos ni a identificar con precisión cada elemento de la vía pública.

Por ello, es fundamental conocer las capacidades y limitaciones de cada dispositivo antes de incorporarlo a las actividades cotidianas.

El Centro de Tiflotecnología e Innovación de la ONCE ha evaluado las gafas inteligentes Ray-Ban Meta y su aplicación Meta AI para analizar su posible utilidad para personas con ceguera o discapacidad visual grave. Su evaluación constituye una referencia especializada para conocer las posibilidades de esta tecnología.

La experiencia de Daniel refleja cómo la combinación de inteligencia artificial, dispositivos inteligentes y herramientas de accesibilidad puede facilitar distintas actividades de la vida diaria.

Sin embargo, la tecnología por sí sola no elimina todas las barreras. Es necesario que las soluciones sean fiables, accesibles y adaptadas a las necesidades reales de las personas con discapacidad visual.

También resulta importante que su desarrollo tenga en cuenta la experiencia de quienes las utilizan. La participación de las propias personas con discapacidad permite identificar necesidades concretas y mejorar la utilidad de estas herramientas.

En definitiva, las gafas inteligentes y la inteligencia artificial representan nuevas oportunidades para acceder a la información y desenvolverse con mayor autonomía. Su utilidad dependerá de que sigan mejorando y se integren como un complemento de los recursos de apoyo ya existentes.

Fuentes: El Periódico: reportaje sobre Daniel Álvarez y las nuevas tecnologías para personas con discapacidad , Centro de Tiflotecnología e Innovación de la ONCE: evaluación de las gafas inteligentes Ray-Ban Meta .

en.title: In-Process 2nd November 2026
en.summary: Happy All Saints Day / All Souls Day (I’m conscious of time zones, it is one of those two days for everyone, depending on where you are in the world). And wherever you are – Happy new NVDA release 🙂 Ok that was last week, but it’s like a birthday, the celebration doesn’t have to… Read More
en.body:
Happy All Saints Day / All Souls Day (I’m conscious of time zones, it is one of those two days for everyone, depending on where you are in the world). And wherever you are – Happy new NVDA release Ok that was last week, but it’s like a birthday, the celebration doesn’t have to end just because the calendar has ticked over This time around, we have:

The exciting news this time around is that NVDA 2026.3 is now available for download. This release includes significant performance improvements, improvements to NVDA’s dialogs, and expanded touch screen input.

Please note: We are aware of an issue for users of Brazilian Portuguese. We will have an update out shortly. Right now, affected users can use the NVDA 2026.3.1 Release Candidate or you can downgrade to NVDA 2026.2 .

Back to NVDA 2026.3: Several performance improvements have been made to reduce lag and improve responsiveness. NVDA now fetches and caches more information about controls in the background, improving performance in controls such as combo boxes and File Explorer. NVDA no longer causes File Explorer or other applications to crash when NVDA is exited or restarted. NVDA now recovers more quickly when an application stops responding, and will no longer freeze or flood the log with errors from unresponsive applications.

Context menus and keyboard shortcuts have been added to the Configuration Profiles, Input Gestures, and Speech Dictionaries dialogs, making these dialogs easier to use with the keyboard. It is also now possible to change an existing gesture directly in the Input Gestures dialog. The dialog used to present browsable messages has been modernized and now better supports resizing, maximizing, and minimizing.

Touch screen input has been significantly expanded. Sequential two-flick gestures now combine two flicks in quick succession into a single gesture, greatly increasing the number of bindable touch gestures. Edge gestures are also now supported, allowing gestures that start from any screen edge to be bound independently from the same gesture performed in the centre of the screen.

A new unassigned command has been added to move the mouse cursor to the centre of the magnified view. Windows OCR can now be used while the Screen Curtain or NVDA’s built-in Magnifier is active.

Liblouis has been updated with new Elfdalian, Sami, Maori, New Zealand Unified English Braille, Haitian Creole braille tables, a Norwegian table for Spanish text, and additional Swedish 6 and 8 dot variants. eSpeak NG has been updated with added support for Ligurian and Abkhaz.

Read the full details and download at: The NVDA 2026.3 Release Announcement .

Last fortnight we mentioned the new “Low Vision Users” page with information on various ways a low vision users might get the most out of NVDA. One big feature for this is, of course, the NVDA magnifier introduced in NVDA 2026.2. The post includes details of that, as well as including a link back to the previous blog post comparing the magnifier with the Windows magnifier , so you can judge which one will best meet your needs.

This week, I thought I’d pick out two other specific sections of that page for a closer look. Firstly, a short tip, but a useful one:

Copying information from web pages Traditionally, NVDA has only the text, not formatting or images, when copying information from web pages . It has also only worked when information was selected with the keyboard. NVDA has an option called “ Native Selection Mode ” which lets users copy formatting as well.

Importantly, if you select text with the mouse and then try to copy it with control+c , this will only work when using “Native Selection mode”. This mode can be toggled for individual pages with NVDA+shift+f10 . In NVDA 2026.3 and later, this mode can be enabled automatically in NVDA’s “Browse mode settings”.

This option in Browse mode settings is new for NVDA 2026.3 so well worth highlighting for anyone who can use it.

Visual Highlighter

NVDA’s Visual Highlight puts a border around the current object with focus, which can highlight what NVDA is reading. Press NVDA+control+g to open NVDA’s settings directly. Press control+tab to move between the different pages of settings. Use control+tab to move to the “Vision” page. The user guide describes the colours. Here are the descriptions: Solid blue highlights a combined navigator object and system focus location (e.g. because the navigator object follows the system focus) Dashed blue highlights just the system focus object Solid pink highlights just the navigator object Solid yellow highlights the virtual caret used in browse mode (where there is no physical caret such as in web browsers)

NVDA is able to move the focus around documents such as web pages where normally navigation doesn’t work. For instance, without NVDA running, you can’t arrow through a word on a web page. NVDA displays a pink line surrounding the current element with focus, such as a heading or paragraph of text. The yellow outline surrounds the character within that element which has focus (Usually the first character, unless you have moved the caret with, for instance, right arrow). A blue line surrounds the current interactive element (something you can press tab to move to). The “Basic Training for NVDA” module has more tips and techniques for navigating with the keyboard.

Screenshot of NVDA’s settings screen with a blue dotted highlight for the system focus around the “Enable Highlighting” option, and a pink highlight for the navigator object around the “Options:” heading. The mouse pointer is larger and coloured (refer to Other Windows Settings below).

We’ve made a couple of small changes to the navbar on the website this week. Hopefully all logical, but worth mentioning just in case: News: We removed the “Newsletter” and “Blog” items and replaced them with “News”. This is a menu which has options to “Subscribe” to news, check out our “Blog”, read “NVDA Stories” from users, or binge “All News Posts”. We’ve removed the “Create Account / Log In” option and in its place, the “Shop” item is a menu which lets you go to “Shop Training & Support”, “Create Account / Log In”, go to your “Cart” and “Download Purchases” (downloadable material you have previous purchased).

In addition, for those who need it, if you activate the header item for any of the navbar items with submenus (About, Get Help, News or Shop), it takes you to a page with links to each of the options for that section. What do you think? If you’ve got any feedback or any concerns, as always, please let us know.

Last fortnight we shared our new “ Accessibility Testing with NVDA ” package. There has been a lot of interest in this, but I did want to cover one question we did get: Does the Accessibility Testing with NVDA package lead into the “NVDA Expert Certification”?

The answer is “No”, as they are aimed at different groups of users:

NVDA Expert Certification is aimed at users who want to prove their screen reader skills (e.g. to potential employers) or professionals who teach or support NVDA users. The exam covers the skills an end user would need to know, but which are not important for accessibility testing. A good training module to lead into this exam is “ Basic Training for NVDA ”. This module teaches things such as how to navigate around text by word, sentence and paragraph, how to search for text on a page, and copy it. It also covers using tools such as OCR or object navigation for getting around places which aren’t as accessible.

“ Accessibility Testing with NVDA ” on the other hand, covers some NVDA skills, but places more emphasis on the information the screen reader is giving you which can help you ascertain the accessibility of your content. This module does not cover the finer points of searching or navigating by word, but notes the way nonvisual users can locate important information on a page, and the kinds of elements which can be useful for this. Instead of covering features for accessing inaccessible content, Accessibility Testing with NVDA highlights ways of checking that your content is accessible, and what to do if it is not.

If you are an accessibility professional who wants a way to show the world that accessibility is important to you and that you do incorporate NVDA in your testing, then we do have good news. The “ Accessibility Testing with NVDA ” package includes a badge you can add to your email signature, your website or elsewhere. We encourage you to display it proudly!

That’s all for this week. We’ll be back in a fortnight with more. Do try out NVDA 2026.3 if you haven’t already. We hope you enjoy the performance and other improvements, and we look forward to sharing more highlights with you soon.

en.title: Set Up ZoomText and Fusion to Work the Way You Do
en.summary: ZoomText and Fusion are powerful accessibility tools designed for people with low vision. ZoomText is a screen magnifier and reader, while Fusion combines all of ZoomText’s features with the full JAWS screen reader, offering both magnification and speech. In honor of National Disability Employment Awareness Month, our Workplace Ready blog series has run throughout October, …
en.body:
ZoomText and Fusion are powerful accessibility tools designed for people with low vision. ZoomText is a screen magnifier and reader, while Fusion combines all of ZoomText’s features with the full JAWS screen reader, offering both magnification and speech.

In honor of National Disability Employment Awareness Month, our Workplace Ready blog series has run throughout October, with a new post every Thursday spotlighting ZoomText and Fusion features that help you be more productive at work. This is the final post in the series. Last week, we shared practical tips for tackling online tasks. This week, we’ll show you how to set up ZoomText and Fusion to work the way you do.

The features we’ve covered this month are most helpful when they’re tuned to the way you work. Taking a few minutes to customize ZoomText and Fusion is one of the most important steps you can take for workplace productivity. The right magnification level, colors, and view for each task mean less time adjusting settings and more time getting things done.

Personalized settings remove the small points of friction that add up over a busy day. When your tools are ready the moment you open an application, you can move between tasks smoothly and work more efficiently and independently. This week, we’ll look at how to save settings for each application, set up your preferred colors and display options, and use touch screen support on compatible devices.

The settings that work well in one program may not be the best choice for another. With Application Settings, you can save unique magnification and enhancement settings for each application you use. Once saved, ZoomText and Fusion automatically load the right settings as you switch between programs, so you don’t have to stop and adjust your view every time you change tasks.

To create Application Settings, open the application and adjust magnification, cursor, or mouse settings to meet your needs, then open the ZoomText menu, choose Application Settings , and save the current settings for that application. To keep your general preferences for every other program, choose Configurations > Save As Default from the ZoomText menu.

Here’s how this might look across a typical workday:

When you move from writing a report in Word to answering email in Outlook, ZoomText and Fusion switch to your Outlook settings automatically. When you come back, your Word settings are right where you left them.

The right colors can make text easier to read and reduce eye strain over a long workday. Color Enhancements let you choose from a variety of preset color schemes, such as inverted brightness or high-contrast combinations, or create your own custom colors. To pick a scheme, select the arrow next to the Color button on the Magnifier toolbar tab. Press CAPS LOCK+C to toggle color enhancements on and off. When you find a combination you like, save it as part of your default configuration or your Application Settings so it’s ready when you need it.

Different tasks also call for different views. ZoomText and Fusion offer several zoom window types for a single monitor: Full , Overlay , Lens , Line , and Docked (Top, Bottom, Left, or Right). Full magnifies the entire screen, which works well for reading documents. Docked keeps part of the screen at normal size, which can be helpful when you want to see the whole layout of an application while magnifying the area you’re working in. Press CAPS LOCK+Z to cycle through the zoom window types, or select the Window button on the Magnifier toolbar tab to choose one.

If you use more than one monitor, ZoomText and Fusion can extend your workspace across two displays. When your monitors are set to extend your desktop, you can choose from these zoom window types:

In the MultiView modes, press CAPS LOCK+V to switch the active view. For more options, such as keeping both views at the same magnification level, select Window > Settings on the Magnifier toolbar tab and choose Multiple Monitor Options .

If you work on a touch screen laptop or tablet, you can control ZoomText and Fusion with gestures. Touch Screen Support works on Windows devices that support at least five simultaneous touch points.

To get started, open the ZoomText menu and choose Preferences > Touch Screen Support > Enable Touch Icon . The Touch Icon lets you switch between two modes:

Double-tap the Touch Icon with one finger to switch modes. To switch for just a moment, hold one finger on the icon, then lift it to return to the previous mode.

In ZoomText Touch Mode, try these gestures:

A few tips can make touch more comfortable at work. Choose a Touch Icon size and color that are easy for you to see from Preferences > Touch Screen Support on the ZoomText menu. Move the icon out of the way by holding one finger on it and dragging it along the edge of the screen. If you share time between a keyboard and touch, keep the icon in Windows Touch Mode when you’re tapping through applications and switch to ZoomText Touch Mode when you want to zoom or pan.

That brings our Workplace Ready series to a close. Throughout October, we’ve explored how ZoomText and Fusion can help you work more productively and independently. Here’s a look back at what we covered:

There’s always more to discover. Take some time to explore additional features and try new settings as your work changes. For tutorials, webinars, and other learning materials, visit our training page. Thank you for following along this month, and keep thriving in your workplace!

Have questions? Email training@vispero.com .

en.title: Apple Introduces Updated iMac and MacBook Pros with Performance and Connectivity Improvements, a Touchscreen for the High-End MacBook Pro, and More
en.summary: On the heels of introducing the 8th generation iPad Mini , Apple this week updated the iMac and MacBook Pro, bringing faster chips, improved connectivity, and, for the first time, a touchscreen to the MacBook Pro. iMac Featuring up to a 12-core CPU, the new iMac with M6, according to Apple's press release , delivers: Up to 2.5x faster performance in apps like Microsoft Excel, compared to iMac with M1, and up to 1.5x faster performance than M4. Up to 3.3x faster graphics performance for tasks including photo editing in Affinity, compared to iMac with M1, and up to 2x faster performance than M4. Up to 12x faster on-device AI performance for prompt processing in LM Studio, compared to iMac with M1, and up to 5x faster performance than M4. Up to 2x higher gaming performance with ray tracing compared to M4. Up to 2x faster SSD read and write performance. With the N1 wireless networking chip, the new iMac supports Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6, and up to a 2.5 gigabit Ethernet port, included with the power adapter. The iMac with M6 is made with 100 percent recycled aluminum in the stand, 100 percent recycled rare earth elements in all magnets, 100 percent recycled gold plating and tin solder in all Apple-designed circuit boards, and is manufactured with 40 percent renewable electricity. It can be pre-ordered from Apple in green, yellow, orange, pink, purple, blue, and silver starting today for a starting price of US $1499, and will begin shipping to customers on Friday, November 6. MacBook Pro In addition to the iMac, Apple updated the base 14-inch MacBook Pro with the M6 chip, N1 wireless networking chip, and up to 170 GBPS of unified memory bandwidth. The MacBook Pro with M6, according to Apple's press release delivers: Up to 13x faster time to first token performance for LLM prompt processing compared to the 13-inch MacBook Pro with M1, and up to 1.3x faster than the 14-inch MacBook Pro with M5. Up to 11.7x faster render performance with ray tracing in Blender compared to the 13-inch MacBook Pro with M1, and up to 1.3x faster than the 14-inch MacBook Pro with M5. Up to 3.3x faster image-processing performance in Affinity compared to the 13-inch MacBook Pro with M1, and up to 1.2x faster than the 14-inch MacBook Pro with M5. Up to 2.5x faster project build performance when compiling code in Xcode compared to the 13-inch MacBook Pro with M1, and up to 1.3x faster than the 14-inch MacBook Pro with M5. Apple also claims the 12-core GPU paired with the dual 16-core neural engine features up to 30 percent faster graphics performance compared to M5, as well as up to 25 percent faster performance for on-device AI workloads. The new MacBook Pro also features the N1 wireless networking chip, bringing Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6 support. The MacBook Pro with M6 is made with 45 percent recycled content overall, including 100 percent recycled aluminum in the enclosure, 100 percent recycled cobalt in the battery, and 100 percent recycled tantalum in multiple capacitors, and is manufactured with 60 percent renewable electricity across the supply chain. It can be pre-ordered from Apple starting today for a starting price of US $1999, and will begin shipping to customers on Friday, November 6. Apple has also introduced new high-end 14 and 16-inch MacBook Pros , bringing a thinner and lighter design, a redesigned thermal architecture, a new speaker design, hinge improvements, and, for the first time on a Mac, an OLED touchscreen and Dynamic Island. With the Dynamic Island, users will be able to view Live Activities, answer calls, and use Siri and Spotlight. At the time of publication, we do not know how VoiceOver or any other macOS accessibility tool will work with touch controls. The MacBook Pro with PROOLEDXDR display continues to use the M5 Pro and M5 Max chips, but it now features a redesigned thermal architecture that Apple claims better redirects air away from the display, helping to prevent it from getting warm to the touch while maintaining sustained performance. The MacBook Pro with PROOLEDXDR display is made with 55 percent recycled content overall, including 100 percent recycled aluminum in the enclosure, 100 percent recycled cobalt in the battery, and recycled tantalum in multiple capacitors, and is manufactured with 45 percent renewable electricity across the supply chain. It can be pre-ordered from Apple starting today for a starting price of US $2899, and will begin shipping to customers on Friday, November 6.

en.title: Real world
en.summary: Welcome to Real World, created by NBM Studios! In this game, players are thrust into a 3D world full of danger and excitement. As a…
en.body:
Published 28 October 2026 by Nr Witta Draco

Welcome to Real World , created by NBM Studios! In this game, players are thrust into a 3D world full of danger and excitement. As a blind player, you must rely on your other senses and quick reflexes to navigate the environment and take down your enemies.

With a variety of weapons at your disposal, including wands for casting spells, you can hunt other players and animals, as well as dragons. If you are lucky enough to defeat the fearsome dragon, you will be rewarded with valuable items and TL, the in-game currency. But beware: the dragon respawns after 30 minutes, giving other players the chance to challenge it.

In addition to intense player-vs-player combat, the game also offers a variety of missions and challenges to complete. You can rob banks and palaces, steal valuable items, and earn extra TL. You can also take on mafia missions and defeat gangsters to earn even more rewards. As you progress through the game, you can even purchase your own hotel and use it as a base of operations. With a dynamic and constantly changing world, no two games are ever the same.

The adventure does not stop there. In Real World, players can also team up with friends and form clans to take on even more challenging missions and quests. For players who want to take their gameplay further, the game also offers a range of paid items and paid accounts that can provide additional advantages in battle.

You can create tickets to request new features or report bugs, and even marry other players if you choose. Whether you prefer to go it alone or fight alongside your clan, the choice is yours. Join the adventure and see if you have what it takes to survive in this thrilling game for blind players!

Free or paid:

Accessibility and User Comments:

Real world is an audio-based game designed with accessibility in mind. It includes a built-in screen reader, so TalkBack is not required while playing.

You can explore different maps, purchase weapons and other items from the in-game store using the game’s currency, and discover different areas featuring animals and other elements.

The app’s user interface is accessible, with no unlabeled buttons reported. The game is easy to use once you learn its touchscreen gestures.

en.title: Announcing AnonyMouse's App Pick of the Month for October 2026: ReSort: Water Sort Puzzle App
en.summary: Welcome to the October 2026 installment of AnonyMouse's App Pick of the Month, where each month I highlight a new or noteworthy app. This month's pick is ReSort: Water Sort Puzzle App, a fun and relaxing water-sorting puzzle game that has quickly become one of my favorites. I know, I know. Another game for my App Pick of the Month! I realize not everyone here is a gamer, and I'm sorry for picking yet another one. But we've had so many fun new games coming our way lately, I just can't help myself! ReSort was simply too much fun to pass up. Maybe next month I'll pick something different. No promises, though! About ReSort ReSort is a puzzle game where you sort different-colored water into separate tubes until each tube contains just one color. Sounds simple enough, right? Well, it starts out that way, but things get trickier as you progress. Before long, you're moving water back and forth, trying to figure out your next move without getting yourself stuck. What I really enjoy is that there's no rush with ReSort. No timers, no move limits, and no pressure. You can take your time and figure things out at your own pace. But don't mistake relaxing for easy! Some puzzles can really get you scratching your head, and finally solving one that's been giving you trouble is incredibly satisfying. There's plenty to keep you busy, too. Along with the regular levels, ReSort offers daily puzzles with different difficulty settings and a larger Sunday challenge. You can also earn stars, work your way through different ranks, and unlock additional sounds as you progress. Accessibility is another reason ReSort stands out. The game was designed with VoiceOver in mind, with announcements for the colors and their positions in each tube. And I have to say, I absolutely love the sounds in this game! From the satisfying sound of pouring water to the little audio cues and gentle music, everything adds to the experience. It's one of those games where the sounds make playing that much more enjoyable. I also love that you can customize them to your liking. Something else I really appreciate is the developer's involvement with the AppleVis community. Since introducing ReSort in the AppleVis forum , the developer has been actively listening to feedback and making improvements. Suggestions from community members have already led to different daily puzzle difficulties, iCloud syncing, more sound options, and adjustable tube sizes for low-vision players. I love seeing developers take our community's suggestions seriously, especially when those suggestions turn into actual features so quickly. It's wonderful to see that kind of engagement. Why I'm Picking ReSort This Month For me, ReSort is just plain fun. It's easy to learn, challenging enough to keep me interested, and relaxing enough to enjoy whenever I have a few minutes to spare. And that's where the trouble starts! I'll tell myself I'm only going to play a couple of levels, and before I know it, I've played several more. There's always another puzzle waiting, and I can't seem to resist finding out whether I can solve it. I also appreciate getting to enjoy this type of game with VoiceOver. Water-sorting games have been around for years, but finding one that's this accessible isn't something I take for granted. Between the enjoyable gameplay, wonderful sounds, thoughtful accessibility, and a developer who's genuinely listening to our community, ReSort has earned its place as my October App Pick of the Month. If you enjoy puzzle games, or just want something relaxing that gives your brain a little workout, I definitely recommend giving ReSort a try. Just don't blame me if you find yourself playing longer than you planned! Download the App ReSort: Water Sort Puzzle App is available on the App Store for iPhone and iPad. The first 10 levels are free, with a one-time purchase to unlock the remaining levels. There are no ads or subscriptions, and all accessibility features are included for free. Now It's Your Turn Have you tried ReSort yet? Are you finding it as addictive as I am? How far have you made it in the game? I'd love to hear what you think and what other apps or games you've been enjoying this month. Let me know in the comments. I always enjoy hearing what everyone else is playing and discovering!

I know, I know. Another game for my App Pick of the Month! I realize not everyone here is a gamer, and I'm sorry for picking yet another one. But we've had so many fun new games coming our way lately, I just can't help myself! ReSort was simply too much fun to pass up. Maybe next month I'll pick something different. No promises, though!

ReSort is a puzzle game where you sort different-colored water into separate tubes until each tube contains just one color. Sounds simple enough, right? Well, it starts out that way, but things get trickier as you progress. Before long, you're moving water back and forth, trying to figure out your next move without getting yourself stuck.

What I really enjoy is that there's no rush with ReSort. No timers, no move limits, and no pressure. You can take your time and figure things out at your own pace. But don't mistake relaxing for easy! Some puzzles can really get you scratching your head, and finally solving one that's been giving you trouble is incredibly satisfying.

There's plenty to keep you busy, too. Along with the regular levels, ReSort offers daily puzzles with different difficulty settings and a larger Sunday challenge. You can also earn stars, work your way through different ranks, and unlock additional sounds as you progress.

Accessibility is another reason ReSort stands out. The game was designed with VoiceOver in mind, with announcements for the colors and their positions in each tube. And I have to say, I absolutely love the sounds in this game! From the satisfying sound of pouring water to the little audio cues and gentle music, everything adds to the experience. It's one of those games where the sounds make playing that much more enjoyable. I also love that you can customize them to your liking.

Something else I really appreciate is the developer's involvement with the AppleVis community. Since introducing ReSort in the AppleVis forum , the developer has been actively listening to feedback and making improvements. Suggestions from community members have already led to different daily puzzle difficulties, iCloud syncing, more sound options, and adjustable tube sizes for low-vision players.

I love seeing developers take our community's suggestions seriously, especially when those suggestions turn into actual features so quickly. It's wonderful to see that kind of engagement.

For me, ReSort is just plain fun. It's easy to learn, challenging enough to keep me interested, and relaxing enough to enjoy whenever I have a few minutes to spare.

And that's where the trouble starts! I'll tell myself I'm only going to play a couple of levels, and before I know it, I've played several more. There's always another puzzle waiting, and I can't seem to resist finding out whether I can solve it.

I also appreciate getting to enjoy this type of game with VoiceOver. Water-sorting games have been around for years, but finding one that's this accessible isn't something I take for granted.

Between the enjoyable gameplay, wonderful sounds, thoughtful accessibility, and a developer who's genuinely listening to our community, ReSort has earned its place as my October App Pick of the Month.

If you enjoy puzzle games, or just want something relaxing that gives your brain a little workout, I definitely recommend giving ReSort a try. Just don't blame me if you find yourself playing longer than you planned!

ReSort: Water Sort Puzzle App is available on the App Store for iPhone and iPad. The first 10 levels are free, with a one-time purchase to unlock the remaining levels. There are no ads or subscriptions, and all accessibility features are included for free.

Have you tried ReSort yet? Are you finding it as addictive as I am? How far have you made it in the game? I'd love to hear what you think and what other apps or games you've been enjoying this month.

en.title: Apple Introduces Updated iPad Mini with Thinner and Lighter Design, Upgraded Display and Camera, A20 Pro chip, N1 and C2 Networking Chips, and More
en.summary: Apple today introduced the new 8th-generation iPad mini, bringing a thinner and lighter design, an 8.5-inch OLED display, A20 Pro chip, N1 and C2 networking chips, a new audio system, and more. With the new design, iPad mini features an upgraded 8.5-inch OLED display while maintaining its existing footprint, thanks to 24 percent thinner bezels. A new audio system that integrates components between the display and enclosure removes the speaker holes and contributes to an IP67 water and dust resistance rating, a first for any iPad. With A20 Pro, Apple claims iPad mini delivers up to 4.5X faster AI performance, up to 2.7X faster graphics performance, and up to 60 percent faster performance for everyday tasks compared to the previous generation. In addition, the N1 wireless networking chip adds Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, and Thread support to iPad mini, and cellular models of the device include Apple's C2 modem, which Apple claims delivers up to 50 percent faster data speeds compared to the previous generation. The 12MP Center Stage front camera has been moved to the landscape edge of the device, as it is on other iPad models. Apple touts this as beneficial for FaceTime calls and collaboration. Apple additionally claims that the new Adaptive True Tone flash improves photos and document scanning. To compliment the new iPad mini, Apple has also introduced a new Smart Folio magnetic cover that features "TechWoven" fabric. The new iPad mini is made with 35 percent recycled content overall, including 100 percent recycled aluminum in the enclosure and 100 percent recycled cobalt in the battery, and is manufactured with 40 percent renewable energy across the supply chain. It can be pre-ordered from Apple starting Wednesday, October 28 in midnight and starlight finishes for a starting price of US $699, and will begin shipping to customers on Friday, November 6.

en.title: Apple Releases iOS 27.2 and iPadOS 27.2 with Expanded Language Support for Siri AI, Profiles for the TV App, Bug Fixes, and More
en.summary: Apple has today released iOS 27.2 and iPadOS 27.2 to the public, bringing Siri AI support for French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish, support for multiple profiles in the TV app, anniversary alerts in Call Context, and various bug fixes. Apple has also released iOS 26.7.2 for devices not running iOS 27. Resolved Accessibility Bugs Our experience is that the following accessibility bugs have been resolved or meaningfully improved in iOS 27.2 and iPadOS 27.2: The changes made to VoiceOver's audio profile in iOS 27.0 and iPadOS 27.0 appear to have been reverted. Using the Dot Pad, The f1 and f4 keys now pan the larger 20x8 display correctly. Also using the Dot Pad, the triangular-shaped buttons now pan the 20-cell display as expected. The gesture, keyboard shortcut, and Perkins-style keyboard commands for Touch and Sound Curtain once again work as expected. Navigating and selecting text with a hardware keyboard is significantly improved. VoiceOver recognizing and speaking when an item state changes or when information has updated is significantly improved, however, the issue may still occur occasionally. The buttons to switch between All and Missed in the Phone app's Classic view, as well as the ones to switch between Start Page, Bookmarks, Reading List, and History in Safari, now work. The "Clear All" rotor action in Notification Center once again works. The "Direct Touch" option in VoiceOver's Quick Settings panel once again works. It is once again possible to swipe from the battery indicator to other items on the status bar when an app is opened. VoiceOver's "copy to clipboard" function now only copies the desired content rather than the full semantic markup. The Call button on the keypad in the Phone app is once again labeled correctly. The "Delete" action in the rotor for conversations in the Siri app is no longer doubled. It is no longer necessary to remove the previously-assigned command in VoiceOver Settings before a new one will work. VoiceOver once again speaks the time at the top of the hour correctly when in 24 hour mode. The "Show Bookmarks" button is once again labeled correctly when the Safari toolbar is set to "Bottom." VoiceOver now works in the "Device Diagnostics" option in the Recovery Menu. The VoiceOver per-voice equalizer now works as expected. VoiceOver once again behaves as expected when editing text and placing focus on a combo box. The Camera App no longer contains extraneous UI elements for editing camera controls when Edit Mode is not active. When swiping through the Lock Screen, VoiceOver focus once again behaves in a consistent and predictable way. In the Camera App, the VoiceOver boundary behavior now works as expected when reaching the first or last element onscreen. New Accessibility Bugs We are currently aware of two new accessibility bugs in these releases: When encountering some emojis and some pictorial icons, VoiceOver speaks them as the words "unspeakable English text." Examples of how this issue may present include: In WhatsApp, you may have a family group name which includes an emoji of adults and children holding hands. Instead of hearing "Family, man, woman and child holding hands emoji", you hear "Family, unspeakable English text". On a website, an icon with a shopping cart may say "Unspeakable English text" instead of "Shopping cart". When navigating content, VoiceOver will on occasion stop speaking, and only provide sounds and haptic feedback. This typically lasts for 20 to 30 seconds. If you notice any further changes, improvements, or regressions in your use of these releases, please post a comment below with your findings. Release Notes iOS 27.2 This update provides enhancements to Siri AI with the ability to retain useful context from previous Siri interactions as well as draw from a wider range of personal context. It also introduces Suggestions in Messages that help you take quick actions in apps like Calendar and Reminders based on context from your conversation. This release includes additional features, bug fixes, and security updates for your iPhone. Siri AI (All iPhone 16 models and later, iPhone 15 Pro, iPhone 15 Pro Max) Siri AI can recall your past conversations, so you can ask Siri about something it told you before, like the restaurants it recommended last week. Siri AI can draw from more sources to give you a great answer, including photos attached in Messages, Calendar event attendees, your voicemails, and better results from Safari history and Reading List. Excluded Apps lets you choose which apps Siri, Search, and suggestions can access, all from one setting. Granular text selection lets you select and copy just the part of a Siri response you need. Siri AI is available in more languages, with support for French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish. Siri AI is not available in the EU or mainland China. Other Suggestions in Messages help you take action based on the context of your conversations, like adding a Calendar invite for a dinner. Shared Albums in Photos adds the ability to edit captions and comments, to avoid adding duplicate photos, and can display a reminder before albums expire so participants can save important photos and videos. Support for SynthID watermarking to help identify whether an image was generated or modified with generative tools in Photos and Image Playground. The Home tab in the Podcasts app offers two separate sections for New Episodes and Continue Playing, letting you find the latest updates from your shows and then pick up where you left off. Friends tab in the Games app provides context on friend suggestions and shows recent games played on friends’ player pages. Simple Profiles in the Apple TV app lets everyone in your household have their own profile, with recommendations that fit what they like to watch. FaceTime supports adding a third party sign language interpreter or live captioner to a call. Shuffle option lets you enjoy different screen saver categories as your Apple TV cycles through them. Find My Find My support lets you locate your Siri Remote (2nd generation) or later using your iPhone. HomePod Software 27.2 HomePod software version 27.2 brings the new Sound Glow visual experience, home theater surround sound with Apple TV 4K (4th generation), and support for using HomePod speakers with your Mac, along with bug fixes and security updates for your HomePod. Sound Glow on HomePod mini, HomePod mini 2, and HomePod (2nd generation) turns the top of HomePod into a visual display that pulses and glows in sync with your media and shows matching light animations for soundscapes. Home theater surround sound supports connecting four HomePod speakers to Apple TV 4K (4th generation) for an immersive listening experience. Requires matching front and rear pairs of HomePod mini 2 or HomePod (2nd generation). HomePod speakers with your Mac lets you set HomePod as the audio output for everything you do on your Mac, with a responsive and persistent AirPlay connection. Lock controls let you disable the touch controls on top of HomePod to prevent accidental taps from pausing music, skipping songs, or changing the volume. If other updates are available, you can click the Info button to see details about them and select specific updates to install. watchOS 27.2 is available via Over-the-Air Update (Settings > General > Software Update) or by going to the Watch app on your iPhone and navigating to General > Software Update. To install the update, your Watch must be connected to its charger and have at least 50% battery power. To install tvOS 27.2, on Apple TV 4K or Apple TV HD, go to the Settings channel, then look for the System section near the bottom. From here, look for Software Updates under Maintenance, then select Update Software and Download and Install. Wait for your Apple TV to download the update. Don't disconnect or unplug your Apple TV until the update completes. By default, HomePod and HomePod mini automatically install new software updates, but you can manually check for updates in the Home app on your iPhone, iPad, or Mac.

Tras 6 versiones beta y una candidata a liberación, NV Access ha anunciado mediante esta publicación que ya se encuentra disponible para su descarga la versión final de NVDA 2026.3, el lector de pantalla gratuito y de código abierto para Microsoft Windows. Se recomienda a todos los usuarios actualizar a esta nueva versión, cuyo uso se considera apto también en entornos de producción.

Esta versión incluye importantes mejoras de rendimiento, mejoras en los cuadros de diálogo de NVDA y una mayor compatibilidad con la entrada mediante pantalla táctil. Se han introducido varias mejoras de rendimiento para reducir el retraso y mejorar la capacidad de respuesta. NVDA ahora recopila y almacena en caché más información sobre los controles en segundo plano, lo que mejora el rendimiento en controles como los cuadros combinados y el Explorador de archivos. NVDA ya no provoca que el Explorador de archivos u otras aplicaciones se cuelguen al salir de NVDA o al reiniciarlo. Ahora, NVDA se recupera más rápidamente cuando una aplicación deja de responder y ya no se bloquea ni satura el registro con errores de las aplicaciones que no responden. Se han añadido menús de contexto y atajos de teclado a los cuadros de diálogo «Perfiles de configuración», «Gestos de entrada» y «Diccionarios del habla», lo que facilita el uso de estos cuadros de diálogo con el teclado. Ahora también es posible modificar un gesto ya existente directamente en el cuadro de diálogo «Gestos de entrada». Se ha actualizado el cuadro de diálogo que se utiliza para mostrar los mensajes que se pueden consultar y ahora permite cambiar el tamaño, maximizar y minimizar con mayor facilidad. Se han ampliado considerablemente las opciones de introducción de datos mediante pantalla táctil. Los gestos secuenciales de dos flicks combinan ahora dos flicks consecutivos en un único gesto, lo que aumenta considerablemente el número de gestos táctiles a los que se pueden asignar acciones. Ahora también se admiten los gestos desde los bordes, lo que permite asociar gestos que se inician desde cualquier borde de la pantalla de forma independiente de los mismos gestos realizados en el centro de la pantalla. Se ha añadido una nueva orden sin asignar para desplazar el cursor del ratón al centro de la vista ampliada. Ahora es posible utilizar el OCR de Windows mientras están activos la Cortina de pantalla o el magnificador integrado de NVDA. Se ha actualizado Liblouis con nuevas tablas de braille en elfdaliano, sami, maorí, braille unificado neozelandés, criollo haitiano, una tabla noruega para texto en español y variantes adicionales suecas de 6 y 8 puntos. Se ha actualizado eSpeak NG para que sea compatible con el ligur y el abjasio. Consulta todas las novedades aquí Tan pronto como actualices NVDA, no olvides reiniciar el equipo. El reinicio garantiza que se pueden actualizar archivos que antes no se podían modificar porque estaban abiertos para escritura. En la práctica, al reiniciar vuelven a funcionar aplicaciones basadas en Electron, tales como Teams, Dropbox o Google Drive, y dejan de producirse comportamientos extraños con el explorador de archivos, Thunderbird, Office y algunos navegadores. Reiniciar es lo primero que debes hacer antes de informar de cualquier fallo. Hazlo pulsando windows+d para ir al escritorio, alt+f4, e intro sobre la opción Reiniciar. Puedes descargar NVDA 2026.3, así como las últimas versiones compatibles con sistemas antiguos y material útil para desarrolladores, desde nuestra página de descargas . La suma SHA256 de NVDA 2026.3, que se usa para garantizar la integridad de la descarga, es a8a87cb823da0c62cfbae4a444ae5ae238d54dc82ad6d46d3fdb3fef082799b2. Si tienes una versión estable anterior, también puedes actualizar automáticamente desde el menú Ayuda. Y desde la rc1, con el complemento Selector del canal de actualización, se puede hacer del mismo modo configurando previamente el canal estable. Si todavía no conoces NVDA y quieres leer algo más sobre él antes de probarlo, te recomendamos consultar la guía de usuario y la referencia rápida de órdenes . Si te gustan nuestros proyectos y el contenido que ofrecemos, plantéate contribuir mensualmente con una pequeña cantidad. Tan sólo un euro es capaz de marcar la diferencia y ayudarnos a mejorar. Visita la página de donaciones para obtener más información, o la tienda para hacerte con libros de formación traducidos y sintetizadores de voz de alta calidad. ¡Feliz lunes!
